# Unabridged Changelog - workspace template

Full, unedited changelog entries consolidated nightly from the individual files in the template's `changelog/` folders (`system/changelog/`, `.agents/changelog/`, and the one in each library, service and app under `system/`).

For a concise summary, see [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md).

## 2026-11-18

### .agents

The `datalib` skill now installs datalib v0.55.0. Search runs on datalib's own index, with qmd gone from the Node runtime, so the first-use download drops from about 195 MB to about 160 MB. The Claude source also downloads Cowork tasks, Baby Connect is a new source, and a person can mute a problem row they have already seen. Raw stores only gain columns and tables (each `problems` table, Claude's Cowork tables), so a reader of an existing store keeps working.

Address user feedback and internal inconsistencies in Latchkey-related skills.

The `manage-desktop` skill no longer describes a placeholder ("ghost") a popped-out window leaves on the desktop, since the desktop now draws nothing there. Its way-back advice is closing the popped-out window or "Bring back to desktop" on its taskbar entry; dragging it back over the Imbue Studio window no longer returns it. The `popped_out` entries keep their `is_ghost_hidden` field, which now only says the placement is also minimized.

Update-self's what's new is the target's root `CHANGELOG.md` section for each release newer than the workspace's, plus `[Unreleased]` when it holds anything. A workspace older than every section is shown them all with a note that earlier releases are not summarized, a workspace whose release cannot be found is shown only the newest release, a target without `CHANGELOG.md` shows nothing, and one whose `CHANGELOG.md` has no release section shows no release; the results message says when any of these applied.

The worker's merge triage takes the target's side for the root `CHANGELOG.md` and `UNABRIDGED_CHANGELOG.md` and for an entry file the target deletes, first saving the workspace's version to another path when it holds text the target's lacks. Converting a user package to a standalone project leaves the root changelogs as written.

### system

The chat-agent-split plan now describes a handoff's switching step in its new order: the retiring agent is renamed to its archival name first, then stopped while the successor is created, and its final event count is recorded once the stop is done. It also describes a landed switch: once the new agent is the chat's last member, the chat reads as that agent and an interrupt waits for the remaining deliveries instead of being refused.

Removed the Claude Stop hook that refused to end a turn until the agent's shell was back at the repo root. Claude Code runs hooks in whatever folder the agent's shell is in. The hook was added to protect hooks that assumed the repo root, but answering it cost the agent a second reply: a `cd`, usually followed by "I'm back at the repo root." In the chat, that reply also broke the turn, so a step left open for the next turn was drawn a second time beneath the hook.

Claude's hooks now name their scripts as `"${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}"/...` instead of falling back to the current folder when `MNGR_AGENT_WORK_DIR` is unset. The scripts that read the repo root fall back to `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` before the current folder. The session-start sync moves to the repo root first, since it also runs after a resume or a compaction. A test checks that every Claude hook command names its files from the project folder. Agents can still `cd` into a folder and keep working there across commands.

The changelog entries of every release through minds-v0.10.5 moved into the root changelogs, and their entry files are gone. `UNABRIDGED_CHANGELOG.md` holds each entry's text under a `## [minds-v<version>] - <date>` section for the first release that carried it, and `CHANGELOG.md` has a summary section for each release from minds-v0.9.5 to minds-v0.10.5. Entries for changes after minds-v0.10.5 stay as files until they are consolidated.

The desktop interface plan, its contracts and concepts notes, and the element reference menu plan state that on a non-touch client the pages of background windows take the pointer, and that the shell raises a window when the document's focus lands in its page, except for a focus the page takes in answer to a message the shell had just sent it; a page that reports its own focus (`shell:focused`) raises its window regardless. The shared `requestFrameFocus` answers a function that drops its pending posts, and takes an `isStillWanted` option that drops a post whose window no longer wants the focus and an `onPosted` option called after each post.

AGENTS.md now says that a long paste the chat turned into an attachment is stored in that chat's own folder, so deleting the chat deletes it.

The desktop-interface blueprint docs (`concepts.md`, `contracts.md`) no longer describe the ghost a pulled-out window used to leave on the desktop: the desktop draws nothing for a detached placement, minimizing one changes nothing on screen, its taskbar entry always shows the window's own desktop window, and `is_ghost_hidden` only carries whether the placement is minimized.

`workspace_ui` gains `isHandledByInputMethod`, which the chat frontend's text fields use to leave the keystrokes of an input-method composition to the input method, so committing a composition no longer sends a message early (see the chat app's entry).

The template has a root `CHANGELOG.md`, a summary that starts with an empty `## [Unreleased]` section and is laid out for one `## [minds-v<version>] - <date>` section per release, and a root `UNABRIDGED_CHANGELOG.md` holding the verbatim entries under the same release headings. The per-change entry files stay in their `changelog/` folders until they are consolidated into the two files.

The changelog gate (`system/scripts/workspace_scripts/check_changelog_entries.py`) asks no entry of a branch whose name starts with `mngr/changelog-consolidation`.

### system/apps/chat

While a chat moves to another harness, the model chip names where it is going (the picked model, or the target's name when none was picked) on every page watching it, instead of showing the model the chat is leaving and then the new agent's settings one write at a time.

Once a handoff's switch has landed on the transcript, the page no longer also shows a second "Handing off to…" spinner below it while the chat finishes delivering to the new agent.

Switching a chat to another provider is quicker: the agent the chat leaves now stops while the new one is created, instead of first. On an idle workspace an empty chat's switch between two Pi accounts went from about 14.4 s to 10.8 s; the saving is however long the old agent takes to stop.

Once a switch has landed on the new agent, the chat reads as that agent while the switch finishes handing it the messages it owes: the status line above the composer shows the agent's own activity instead of "Starting …", the chat list shows its real status, the composer has its usual placeholder, and Stop is offered for its turn. A Stop pressed then waits on the server for those messages to be delivered before it interrupts, so none is lost to the restart.

A switch now says what it is doing in one place: its line in the conversation, which shows each phase ("Wrapping up with Claude Code…", "Claude Code is writing a summary…", "Starting Codex…", or "Restarting … on …" when only the account changes). The line above the message box no longer repeats it, and a chat with nothing to hand over, or one moving to another account, gets that conversation line too instead of a line by the composer.

The harness contract notes state the rule for Claude hooks: a hook names its files from `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}` and never from the folder it runs in. A hook that wants to know where the agent's shell is reads the `cwd` field of its input. The notes also explain why the former repo-root Stop hook was removed.

A Claude chat shows the progress updates Claude 5 models write between tool calls (a sentence or two on what the agent found and what it does next). The API returns each one as a thinking block marked as a progress update, so the chat dropped them, including the ones that carried the turn's actual reply or a decision the user was meant to see. They now read as the agent's prose at their place in the turn, in the progress view, the live reply draft and the chat feed. Reasoning blocks stay hidden.

A very long paste into the chat composer becomes an attachment instead of filling the box.

- A paste of at least 4,000 characters or 80 lines is uploaded as `pasted-text-1.txt` (numbered per message) and shows as a chip saying "Pasted text, N lines"; anything typed stays in the box. The agent is sent the typed words with a link to the file, so every harness reads the whole text.

- The pasted file is stored in the chat's own folder, not the workspace's `data/uploads/`, so deleting the chat deletes it too.

- The chip's "Paste as text" button puts the text back where the caret is and removes the attachment.

- The sent message names the paste by its file name, a link that opens it in Files, rather than by its full path.

The composer no longer sends on the Enter that commits an input-method composition. With a Chinese, Japanese or Korean IME, pressing Enter to commit a Latin word typed through it sent the draft with the uncommitted letters still in it (for example `wo'r'k's'pa'ce`); the box kept the text, so the next Enter sent the whole message again, and the receiver got a partial message and then the full one. Keystrokes that belong to a composition now go to the input method, and the composer sends only on an Enter outside one. The chat rename field, the account rename field and the send-to-chat picker get the same guard, so committing a composition no longer saves a half-typed name or picks a chat.

### system/apps/system_interface

The profile test for stale entries after sharing stops no longer fails at random: it holds the background refresh until its assertions are done, so the refresh's wall-clock timestamp cannot make the entry fresh under them.

The floating avatar (and any pinned app's floating entry) is named after its app on hover, "Chat" for the chat, rather than after the page its window is on, which for the chat was the name of whichever chat was open.

Hovering a window behind the focused one and scrolling now scrolls its page, with no click first. A click or press on a background window reaches its page and brings the window to the front in the same press, as in a native desktop application; before, a transparent cover took that first press and only raised the window. Keys typed after the press go to the window that came forward.

The shell raises a window whenever the document's focus lands in its page, so this holds for every app, whether or not it speaks the shell contract. It reads where the focus is when its own window loses it and on a timer every 100 ms (a tick), so a press that moves the focus from one page to another raises the window within a tick. A focus that reaches a page after a message the shell just sent it (it is shown, or a terminal is asked to take the focus), and that the shell reads within two ticks of that message, is no press to the shell, which hands it back: a page that sends no focus report of its own for it, such as a terminal-like page focusing its nested frame after a reload, a desktop switch or an agent's refresh, stays behind the window you are in. A page that reports its own focus (`shell:focused`, sent by the first-party pages when their window gains focus) raises its window regardless. The focus requests the shell posts to a raised window are dropped once another window is focused, and none goes out while a press into another window's page is waiting to raise that window. A click that a page cancels, such as one in the chat while its own menu is open, does not move the focus, so that window comes forward on the next click. After the shell raises a window on seeing a focus landing it raises no other that way for three ticks, so pages that take the focus back whenever they lose it no longer flip the stack on every press.

Touch screens keep the cover over background windows, so the first tap there still only raises the window, and every window is covered while a menu or the launcher is open, so the press that closes them never reaches a page.

When the memory guard stops a program to free memory, Imbue Studio no longer gets a notification about it. Freeing memory needs nothing from the user (an update already in progress, for instance, carries on by itself), and a notification invited them to start the stopped program again. The tray's resource card still lists the programs stopped in the last day, and the low-disk, low-memory and busy-CPU warnings still notify as before.

A window pulled out into its own Imbue Studio window no longer leaves a ghost on the desktop. Its place on the desktop stays empty while it is out; its taskbar entry stays, marked as pulled out, and offers "Show" and "Bring back to desktop" in its menu. Closing the window's own Imbue Studio window still brings it back where it was.

- The ghost's "Show", "Hide" and "Bring back" buttons go with it, and so do the taskbar entry's "Hide placeholder" / "Show placeholder" rows. Clicking a pulled-out window's taskbar entry always shows its own window, even when its placement is also minimized (as one whose placeholder was hidden is).

### system/libs/workspace_layout

The `is_ghost_hidden` field of a client's `popped_out` entries is described as what it now carries, whether the pulled-out window's placement is also minimized, since the desktop no longer draws a ghost for a pulled-out window. The field keeps its name.

### system/libs/workspace_ui

`keybindings.ts` exports `isHandledByInputMethod(event)`, which says whether an input method is handling a keydown (a composition is open), by the keydown's `isComposing` flag. A text field calls it before acting on Enter, Escape, Tab or the arrows, and leaves the key alone when it is true.

### system/services/oom_priority

The revival-notice SessionStart hook finds the shed ledger from `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` before the folder it runs in, and hands that location to its Python half. Claude Code runs hooks in whatever folder the agent last `cd`ed to, so a session resumed with its shell in a subfolder could miss the notice when neither `OOM_PRIORITY_RUNTIME_DIR` nor `MNGR_AGENT_WORK_DIR` was set.

## 2026-11-17

### system

`system/libs/workspace_voice/` (a member of the npm workspace, filed here as it has no project of its own) gains `speechModel.ts`, one managed speech model load per engine for the page, built on `@tanstack/query-core` (a new dependency of the library, so `system/package-lock.json` changes with it) and kept in step across the workspace's pages by the engine worker, which now tells each page what it holds as the page connects. `Dictation` no longer loads the model (its `loading` state and `onProgress` are gone), a page can ask whether the model's files are already on this device (`probeEngineDownload`, over the device pick now in `devicePick.ts` and the store's new `has`), and there is a ready chime; see the library's own entry under `system/libs/workspace_voice/changelog/`. The chat's composer uses them for its redesigned mic (see the chat's entry), and the chat frontend declares `@tanstack/query-core` itself, which adds one line to `system/package-lock.json`.

`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` names Moonshine Tiny beside Moonshine Base as a speech model the chat's dictation downloads: the one a phone or tablet runs (see the chat's and the voice library's own entries).

The desktop interface's and the workspace app model's contracts say that `uses_microphone` now also hands an app's frames the screen wake lock, which the chat's dictation holds on a phone (see the chat's and the shell's own entries).

The desktop-interface and workspace-app-model blueprint contracts, and the Routines spec (section 10.1), now list Files and Routines among the manifests that declare `system = true`, and say what follows from the flag: the share panel lists such an app under System, and the desktop app's home screen does not count it among the workspace's own apps.

### system/apps/chat

The composer's mic says when the speech model has to be loaded, and shows the load, in place of the 2 px progress ring users missed. The model's load and dictation are now two things, and the mic shows one of six states, named by its `data-dictation-state`: `load-needed` (the model is not loaded: the glyph sits faint with a warning badge on its corner, and the tooltip names what a press has to do first, `Dictate after a one-time 239 MB download (Cmd+Shift+M)` with the size this device would download, or `Dictate once the speech model has loaded (Cmd+Shift+M)` when the files are already on the device), `loading` (the load is shown: the mic eases into a `Loading voice model` label with the download's progress as a bar under it, and the box around it is left as it is, the text box live), `ready` (the model is loaded, and a press dictates at once, with no loading step on the way), and `starting`, `listening` and `stopping`. A press on a `load-needed` mic means the whole of it: the model is loaded, the load is shown, and dictation begins as soon as the load ends, with no second press. Two short bell tones say when the microphone is open.

A shown load can be dismissed, which calls off the dictation it was to go on to and leaves the load running: a press on the label (a button, which takes the keyboard's focus from the fading mic), Escape, the mic's shortcut, text entered into the box, or the page going out of view. A press or a tap in the text box alone dismisses nothing: it only sets where the dictated words will land. A press right behind the one that asked for the load is taken for that press landing twice and dismisses nothing, and a held shortcut's repeats do nothing. After a dismissal made on the label, with the shortcut or with Escape, the text box takes the focus on a desktop. While a dismissed load runs on the mic reads `load-needed`, a press shows the label again at the load's progress, and the mic turns `ready` without a sound when the load ends; a failure after a dismissal is not told, while a failure of a shown load is told in the notice, whose Retry asks again and which comes down by itself once the model is loaded. The model is the page's and is kept in step across the workspace's pages: a model that another chat panel loaded turns this one's mic `ready` too. Until a page has found out the model's state as its composer mounts (five seconds at most) the mic is drawn `ready`, so a loaded model never flashes the badge. The screen wake lock a dictation holds is held while a load is shown as well. The chat frontend declares `@tanstack/query-core`, which the voice library already installs, as a dependency of its own.

A message that may hold dictated words now tells the model so. Once dictation has written words into the composer, the message sent from that draft ends with a short note, in a `<dictation-note>` tag pair after the words, saying that parts of it were transcribed from speech and may be misheard, so the model reads a word that does not fit as the word or identifier it sounds like, without remarking on it, and asks only when two readings would lead to different actions. The note stays with a draft through edits and partial deletes, and goes once the box is emptied or the message is sent; a message that reads as a slash command or bash-mode input is sent without it. The note is for the model alone: the chat's bubbles (sent, sending, queued and held) show only the person's words, the tray's notification bubbles, the owner's mention notification and the automatic chat title leave it out, and a message that comes back to the composer (a failed send, queued messages returned by Stop or by a switch) comes back as its words alone, with the note added again when it is next sent.

Dictation on a phone or tablet (a page whose primary pointer is a finger) runs Moonshine Tiny, the lighter speech model, in place of Moonshine Base: a third of the download and under half the time per utterance, so the words keep up with the speaker. A desktop keeps Moonshine Base. A browser's `workspace-voice:engine` override still picks any registered engine on either.

On a phone or tablet the model also runs on WebAssembly's quantized weights even where the browser has WebGPU, so the page keeps a third of the memory the full-precision weights would take.

Dictation keeps a phone's screen awake. A phone dims and locks after its idle timeout, speaking is not a touch, and a locked screen hides the page, which stopped dictation mid-sentence. The composer now holds a screen wake lock from the moment a dictation starts loading until it is idle again, asks for it again when the page comes back into view (the browser drops it while the page is hidden), and lets it go when the composer leaves. Best effort: a browser without the API, a frame without the grant, or a refusal such as low battery leaves the screen timing out as before, with nothing shown. The chat root's inner frames allow `screen-wake-lock` beside the microphone.

### system/apps/files

Files is declared a system app (`system = true` in its manifest): it is part of every workspace rather than an app built on it, so the share panel lists it under System and the desktop app's home screen does not count it among the workspace's own apps.

### system/apps/routines

Routines is declared a system app (`system = true` in its manifest): it is part of every workspace rather than an app built on it, so the share panel lists it under System and the desktop app's home screen does not count it among the workspace's own apps.

### system/apps/system_interface

The shell adds `screen-wake-lock` beside `microphone` to the frames of an app whose manifest declares `uses_microphone`, so the chat's dictation can keep a phone's screen awake while it listens. Frames of other apps are handed neither.

### system/libs/workspace_voice

`speechModel.ts` is the page's speech models: one managed load per engine, held in a TanStack Query cache (the new `@tanstack/query-core` dependency). `getSpeechModels()` is the page's one instance and `getVoiceQueryClient()` its query client. A surface observes an engine's load with a `QueryObserver` over `loadQueryOptions(options)` given `enabled: false`, asks for it with `request(options)` (one load runs however many ask, a load in flight is joined, and a loaded model is answered from the cache), reads the download's progress under `progressQueryKey(options)`, finds out what the workspace's worker already holds with `discover(options, isDownloaded)`, and transcribes on `engine(options)`. The engine worker is the authority, and is what keeps the workspace's pages in step: it now tells each port what it already holds as the port connects (a `hello` message); `EngineWorkerClient` gains `onMessage` (every message the worker sends the port, among them each step of a load another page asked for) and `onLost` (the worker taken for lost, which the page's own `dispose` is not); and the speech models mirror what the port hears into the cache, so a page learns a model came ready whichever page asked for it. A page also hears on a BroadcastChannel that another page asked for a model, and connects to hear the worker load it. `isEngineWorkerShared()` says whether the realm's worker is the one every page shares.

`Dictation` no longer loads the speech model. Its `loading` state and its `onProgress` event are gone: `DictationState` is `idle`, `starting`, `listening` or `stopping`, and `start()` goes straight to `starting` and expects the model to be loaded, which a composer asks the page's speech models for first (`getSpeechModels().request(options)`). A dictation transcribes on the page's shared port to the engine worker (`getSpeechModels().engine(options)`) in place of a client of its own, so `dispose()` leaves that port open; `DictationDeps.connect` takes the dictation's options and is asked at every job, so a port connected after a loss is the one used. `describeSpeechModelLoadError(error)` turns what a failed request for the model rejected with into the `DictationProblem` a composer shows, and `isSpeechModelLoadProblem(problem)` tells such a problem from the microphone's and from held words.

`probeEngineDownload` tells a page whether the speech model's files are already on this device: the device picked as the worker picks it (`pickDevice`, now in `devicePick.ts` with the navigator as a parameter) and every pinned file of that variant looked for in the page's own Cache Storage, with the size the download would be; `PinnedFileStore` gains `has(url)` for it. `createReadyChime` plays two short bell tones through the Web Audio API, woken from a user gesture and played when dictation starts listening.

Moonshine Tiny joins the engine registry (`voice_models.json`), pinned at the onnx-community export's commit with every file's size and SHA-256, and the registry now names the engine each kind of device runs by default: Moonshine Base on a desktop, Moonshine Tiny on a touch device (a phone or tablet), each checked at load to be a registered engine offered there. `pageDictationOptions` takes the page's device class and picks that default; the browser's `localStorage` override still wins on every device. Tiny downloads 32 MB on WebAssembly (q8) and 113 MB on WebGPU (fp32), against Base's 67 MB and 251 MB, and transcribes an utterance in under half the time, which is what dictation from a phone's browser needed.

A touch device also insists on the WebAssembly variant (the q8 weights) even where it has WebGPU, unless the browser's `workspace-voice:device` override names a device: the full-precision WebGPU weights take about three times the memory, which is more than a phone's browser gives a page before it kills it. A desktop still lets the worker pick.

## 2026-11-16

### .agents

- The build-app skill's verify step says where the chat's test gate goes: to the background after the app is on screen, with the reply not waiting for it. It used to say the gate was not part of the chat turn at all, which disagreed with `AGENTS.md`.

### system

- `AGENTS.md` tells a chat to start its background test gate last, once the change is on the user's screen, and to reply without waiting for it: the gate's report wakes the agent, and what it finds is a follow-up fix. Chats were holding the reply for the gate, or ending the turn on "running final checks".

- `AGENTS.md` states the rule the pipe guard enforces (no pipe of a command's output into `head` or `tail`, with the two ways around it), so an agent no longer learns it from a rejected tool call.

- `AGENTS.md` tells an agent that is waiting on a command (a long pull of outside data, a sync, a build) to run it in the background and carry on with work that does not need its result, instead of ending the turn or running it in the foreground. Agents building an app over live data were sitting out each full pull.

### system/apps/chat

Automatic chat names stay short. The model that names a new chat is now told to name the message's one main subject as tersely as it can while still saying what the chat is about, in fewer than 40 characters and preferably far fewer, and to leave out the tools, sources and steps a long message lists, with that repeated at the end of the question. Before, a detailed first message could draw a title over 40 characters ("Information flow diagram for Obsidian and output apps"), which was thrown away, so the chat kept "Chat N" until the next message was sent. A title that still runs past 40 characters is now cut at a word and ends in "..." ("Information flow diagram for Obsidian..."), and the cut is logged as a warning.

Deleting a chat now takes it off the list the moment you confirm, rather than crossing it out while the delete runs. If the chat was on screen you move to the next one straight away; if the delete is refused, the chat comes back and the reason is shown. Deleting the last chat clears the list at once, and the new empty chat opens once the delete has gone through.

Renaming a chat now updates the window's title at once, along with the list, rather than when the next chat list arrives. A chat still waiting for its first message or still starting shows its name in the window's title too, rather than "Chats".

## [minds-v0.10.5] - 2026-11-17

### .agents

A new app built with `build-app` is no longer given port 8091, the Screen's video server port. Taking it broke the Screen and the agent browser until the app was moved. An update now moves an existing app off 8090 or 8091, the Screen's two ports.

### system

Installing the frontend dependencies no longer downloads onnxruntime's CUDA binaries from GitHub. `onnxruntime-node` (pulled in by `@huggingface/transformers` in `libs/workspace_voice`) ships its CPU binaries in the npm package, but on Linux x64 its postinstall script also fetches the CUDA execution provider from the onnxruntime GitHub release. When that URL started answering 404 on 2026-11-17, every `npm ci` on Linux x64 failed, which broke CI's frontend step, the image's dependency install, and update-self's frontend refresh.

The new `system/.npmrc` sets `onnxruntime-node-install-cuda=skip`, the value onnxruntime-node's install script documents for skipping that download. Every install of the npm workspace runs in `system/`, so all of them read it. The Dockerfile copies it in alongside the manifests for the dependency layer, and the offload configs list it as a checkpoint build input. Nothing in the workspace uses a GPU, so it loses nothing. npm 11 prints an "Unknown project config" warning for the key but still passes it to the install script.

## [minds-v0.10.4] - 2026-11-13

### .agents

The `datalib` skill now installs datalib v0.53.0. Each message of a document renders on its own, so one message's unclosed code block or stray markup no longer spills into the next, and a message's time is shown on its sender's clock. Claude and ChatGPT syncs can keep a conversation deleted upstream, Fastmail fetches mail in larger batches, and search by meaning keeps answering while a sync writes the index. No stored data changes shape.

The `datalib` skill now installs datalib v0.54.1. Every source re-renders once after the upgrade. A plain-text email now shows as typed, not run through the HTML converter. A name a person reads loses invisible direction marks, and one message can no longer rename a contact everywhere. The search applet's `/sql` binds parameters by name and reads any store a page at a time, a source's documents can be removed in bulk, and links opened from a message send no Referer. No raw store changes shape.

The `migrate-workspace` skill now leaves the old workspace's published share behind: its data copy excludes the share's identity files (`share.env`, `share_auth_label`, `share_gateway_signing_key`, `share_grants.toml` and its lock, `share_identities.json`, `share_tls/`, `agent_access/`) beside the backup and tunnel secrets, through a new `data-excludes` subcommand that owns the list. Copying them made the new workspace present the old one's hostname and certificate, with two machines claiming one share.

Chat recreation works for the chats a workspace has. `recreate-agents` selects the harness with `--type` (the old `--template claude` named a template the workspace does not define), binds each chat to the account it ran on the way the chat app does, with the chat app's `account` label, and recreates an agent that worked in a folder outside the checkout in that folder. `list-agents` reports each agent's harness, account and work folder, finds claude sessions under the account folders, and enumerates codex agents' rollouts. The skill gains an accounts step, inventories the directories outside the checkout and the gitignored files creations depend on, asks for `minds-workspaces-destroy` only at the close-out, and checks that the new workspace is backed up before the old one is stopped.

The notify-user script now also shows each notification on the workspace's desktop, as a bubble over the agent for everyone not looking at the chat, whether or not the Imbue Studio app takes it. When the chat app cannot show it, the script prints a warning and the exit code is unchanged. A garbled answer to a POST now counts as unreachable instead of crashing the script.

- update-self now restarts the workspace's agents when an update changes what their harness processes loaded at start. Before, the apply restarted only the services, so after a Claude Code upgrade (or a change to pi's extensions, as in the pi guards change) every open chat and background agent kept running the old version until something else restarted it.

- Whether a restart is needed is decided by rule and reported (worker guide §4d, a new **Agent restarts** report field the lead's audit requires). The new `update_self.py agent-restart-verdict` reads the mechanical part off the diff: a harness version pin in `setup_system.sh` or `[agent_types.*] version`, the `AGY_VERSION` the Antigravity installer pins, and `.pi/extensions/`. The worker judges only harness config the command cannot place, counting it as loaded at start when its live reload cannot be established. `.claude/settings.json` (Claude Code reloads it live), the scripts hooks run, and an agent's launch config (recorded when the agent is created, so a restart would not pick it up anyway) do not need one.

- After a successful apply the lead runs the new `update_self.py restart-agents`, which asks the chat app to restart every chat and background agent that has ended its turn. The chat app checks each one at the moment of its restart. Conversations carry over. Agents that are working, waiting on a dialog, mid-handoff, receiving a message, holding queued messages, waiting on their harness's own background work (a background shell, a subagent, which a restart would end with no report), or in a state the chat app cannot read are left running and named in the results message, which asks whether to interrupt them. A restart does end a `run_in_background.py` command an idle chat was waiting on, and the chat gets that command's report saying so. A chat or background agent the pass paused for the apply and started again after the update landed already runs what it installed, so `restart-agents` leaves it alone; the run record marks each one the resume started after the update landed. Chat rooms, whose agent runs no harness, are left alone too.

- As its last command the lead runs `update_self.py restart-self`, which restarts the update's own chat once its final turn ends and sends it a note, shown to the user as a one-line notice, asking it to confirm the restart and to repeat the offer for the chats not restarted; when the restart does not happen, the note says so instead.

### system

Chat agents now act on hook feedback (a Stop hook blocking the turn, a reminder attached to a tool call) without mentioning it to the user. One line in `AGENTS.md`, next to the rule against naming the machinery.

The root project overrides paramiko to 5.0.1, the version mngr pins for CVE-2026-44405. pyinfra, which mngr also depends on, caps paramiko below 5 until its 3.11.0 release clears the two-week cooldown, so without the override no mngr commit from 2026-11-12 on could be locked and the twice-daily pin bump failed.

The mngr pin moves to the public mirror of mngr `main` at a0b3ec6c6e, the first pin that needs the override. paramiko goes from 3.5.1 to 5.0.1 in the lock.

Codex chats now run at the speed their fast-mode setting asks for. Before this, the agent terminal's codex TUI could undo the setting whenever it attached: on a new chat, and after every restart. Codex keeps a thread's speed tier when it rebuilds the thread (when the TUI attaches, and on restart), so a tier set by a switch now holds.

- `[agent_types.codex]` no longer pins `service_tier = "default"`, and the `fast` create template no longer sets a codex tier. The TUI re-sent any configured tier when it attached, which undid a fast switch made before it attached, and turned an auto chat that had already dropped to standard speed back to fast after a restart.

- A codex chat that launches fast (fast mode on, or auto with its fast turns still to run) has fast mode turned on by the chat app with a model switch once its agent is up, both for a new chat and for a handoff's successor.

- A turn typed directly in the agent terminal on a model whose default is the fast tier (GPT-6 Sol) now runs fast, and the model bar shows it.

- Moved the Lima guest image (`[providers.lima]` `default_image_url_*`) to the Debian 13 genericcloud `20261103-2651` release (`linux` 6.12.115-2), matching the `mngr_lima` library default and the gen-2 slice guest image. Its kernel carries the btrfs chunk-allocation fix the slice VMs need before they turn on automatic reclaim of sparse data block groups.

The workspace's mngr moves to the `minds-v0.10.4` release of mngr: the pin in `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` names the public mirror commit of the mngr the 0.10.4 desktop app ships, so a workspace built from this tag runs the same mngr the app drives it with.

`system/scripts/agent_resource_notice.sh` is a new prompt hook for claude and codex agents (`.claude/settings.json`, `.codex/hooks.json`): while the workspace is short of disk, memory or CPU it adds the resource monitor's notice to the agent's context. The lock file records that the workspace shell now depends on `disk-headroom` and `oom-priority`.

The desktop-interface contracts describe the `kind` on `POST /api/bubbles` and the `bubble` push (`message` or `notification`), the new loopback `POST /api/chats/<chat-id>/notification` the notify-user script calls, and that only a notification or a mention of the viewer raises a speech bubble.

The harness binaries baked into the workspace image move to their current releases: Claude Code 2.1.323 (was 2.1.307), whose `fable` alias resolves to Claude Fable 5.2; Codex 0.169.0 (was 0.161.0), whose bundled catalog adds GPT-6.1 Terra; OpenCode 1.19.5 (was 1.19.4); and the Antigravity CLI (`agy`) 1.5.8 (was 1.4.7), pinned to the 1.5.8 release URLs and sha512 checksums from Google's release manifest. Each agent type's `version` in `.mngr/settings.toml` moves with it. New codex agents still start on GPT-6.1 Sol. The pi coding agent stays on 0.87.1. Existing workspaces pick the new binaries up from a normal update, which re-runs the provisioner.

- `message_chat.py --interrupt` restarts a chat's agent through the chat app's interrupt route, which replaces its process (the conversation carries over, and anything queued for the agent is resent), then sends the message if one was given. A refusal, such as a chat mid-handoff, is final. Only when the chat app cannot take the restart does `mngr start --restart --no-resume` do it, with `mngr message` carrying the text. update-self offers it for restarting a chat an update left on the previous version.

### system/apps/chat

A codex chat that launches fast (fast mode on, or auto with its fast turns still to run) now gets fast mode from a model switch once its agent is up, for a new chat and for a handoff's successor, instead of from a speed tier in codex's config. A configured tier was re-sent every time codex's agent terminal attached, so an auto chat that had already dropped to standard speed went back to fast after a restart. Claude chats still launch fast through the `fast` create template.

The composer drops NUL characters from a message before sending it. They arrive invisibly when binary content is pasted (a devtools "Copy response" of a binary reply, for instance), and the agent's terminal cannot take them, so such a message used to fail to send.

The new `POST /api/chats/<chat-id>/notification` (loopback only, `{"message", "title"}`) takes each notification the notify-user script sends and posts it to the shell as a `notification` bubble over the agent's tray entry, titled with the chat's title. The agent's turns in an agent chat are no longer posted to the tray at all: each text block of a turn was its own post, so the agent's bubble filled with mid-turn narration. Its posts into a room still are, now naming the people they @-mention, whose clients raise them as a bubble. Every other post is marked a `message`, which the shell raises as a bubble only on the clients of the people it mentions.

The model bar's Fable entry is now Fable 5.2, which Claude Code 2.1.323's `fable` alias resolves to, and it offers fast mode: Fable 5.2 is the first Fable whose baked catalog entry carries the `fast_mode` capability. Fable 5.1 joins the hidden options, so a chat still on it shows its name, and Mythos 5.2 (which also has fast mode) is recognized the same way. The baked Claude model catalog and the binary's model id list are regenerated from the 2.1.323 executable.

- The interrupt route (`POST /api/chats/<id>/interrupt`) takes `{"only_if_idle": true}`: it then restarts the chat only if its agent has ended its turn, and otherwise answers 409 with `busy_with` saying what the chat is doing (working, waiting on a dialog, receiving a message, holding queued messages, waiting on background work, or in a state the chat app cannot read). A chat waiting on its harness's own background work counts as busy, since a restart would end that work with no report; one waiting only on `run_in_background.py` commands does not. update-self uses it to restart the workspace's idle chats after an update that changes their harness, leaving busy ones for the user to decide about.

- It also takes `{"keep_queue": true}`: the messages queued for the agent are resent to it as one turn after the restart, as the flush does, instead of being dropped with the process. `message_chat.py --interrupt` always asks for it.

### system/apps/system_interface

Clicking the agent's avatar in the taskbar's tray now puts the pinned chat window back on screen on whatever chat it was showing: restored if minimized or closed for this client, raised if behind other windows, its own desktop window shown if pulled out, and left alone if already on top. It no longer replaces the open chat with the main chat. Only when the desktop has no pinned chat window does the click open the main chat, as before.

The taskbar's tray has a resource gauge that says how much room the workspace has left.

- When the disk, memory or CPU runs short, the tray shows a warning in words ("Disk space is low"). Resting the pointer on it opens a card: what each resource has left ("3.2 GB left of 44 GB, full in about 12 minutes"), and the programs stopped to free memory in the last day. Clicking the warning or a row opens System Monitor on that resource.

- "Resource gauge..." on the desktop's right-click menu (also on the gauge and its card) is the owner's settings: show three small CPU, RAM and Disk bars always or nothing until a warning, and each warning's level. The disk warns when 5 GB or less is left (and whenever it is on course to fill within 15 minutes); memory and CPU warnings are off until turned on.

- A warning sends one Imbue Studio notification, which opens System Monitor on that resource. It is retried until delivered and is not repeated by a restart. A program the memory guard stops is reported the same way.

- While a warning stands, claude and codex agents are told at their next message, so they hold off on large writes or memory-heavy work and tell the user.

- The gauge is pushed to the windows over the shell's socket; a gauge that stops arriving is drawn as not updating rather than left showing its last figures.

The speech bubbles over the taskbar's tray now show only what is meant for you: a chat's notification to the user (over the agent's entry, on every client not looking at that chat, timing out after five seconds like any bubble) and a message that mentions you, from a person, a visiting agent, or the agent's post into a room (marked, and kept until dismissed or its chat is opened). Any other message still makes its sender's entry hop but raises no bubble. The `bubble` push carries a new `kind` (`message` or `notification`).

### system/apps/system_monitor

A resource warning from the taskbar's resource gauge opens System Monitor on the resource's view (the `minds:show-system-monitor` message, naming `cpu`, `memory` or `disk`).

### system/libs/workspace_layout

`BubblePost` carries a `kind` (`BubbleKind`: `message`, the default, or `notification`), so the shell can tell a chat's notification to the user from a message somebody sent.

### system/services/oom_priority

A local Docker workspace no longer sheds its apps and its own backups when its memory cap fills with file cache.

Under runc the memory guard reads the workspace's headroom from the container's cgroup, and it counted only the inactive file cache as reclaimable. Everything a container reads is charged to its cgroup and stays cached up to the cap, and a file read twice moves to the active list, so a workspace whose hourly backup walks a large tree (a million small files is enough) showed under 10% available while its processes held a sixth of the cap. earlyoom then stopped apps, and the backup itself, every hour, and no backup completed.

The headroom now also counts the active file cache that no process has mapped and the reclaimable slab (the inode and directory-entry caches a tree walk leaves behind), which are what the kernel frees before it kills anything in the cgroup. Mapped file pages are still not counted. Workspaces under gVisor are unaffected: their VM publishes the figure, and a sandbox's file cache stays on the inactive list.

## [minds-v0.10.3] - 2026-11-09

### .agents

An app's crystallize pass now checks how the app works from a phone and when it is shared, right after the worker's first milestone, so the hardened core reaches the user first. The worker drives the app at phone sizes with touch (viewport tag, no sideways scroll, nothing reachable only on hover, tappable controls), fixes what it finds without changing the desktop layout the user confirmed, and commits a phone-sized browser test. It then reviews what a visiting person or agent can reach, against what an app can actually enforce: the app gains the request guard the built-in apps already have, a route that reveals a secret or credential answers visitors 403 on the server, content a visitor saves is rendered safely, changes made through the app record the requester's participant key, an app visitors can change keeps a bounded access log, and neither route descriptions nor the report claim more protection than that. The worker's `done` report gains `Phone:` and `Sharing:` lines, and anything on them it could not fix becomes a ticket. `web-frontend-testing.md` now points browser tests in the repo-root suite at its `module_browser` and `phone_context` fixtures rather than pytest-playwright's `page`, `context` and `browser`, which that conftest refuses, and a user-built app's own suite adds Playwright to its dev group and launches Fortress by its path.

An update's pre-flight check now boots the shell with its state and presence folders in a throwaway directory, so the check never leaves files in the workspace's source tree for the next update to refuse as uncommitted changes.

- The vendored `imbue-studio` skill now tells an agent how to create a workspace where and as large as it should be: `launch_mode`, the connection (`cloud_account`), `instance_type` and the root `disk_gb` for the VM modes, read off the agent's own workspace entry in `GET /api/v1/workspaces` unless the user asks for a different machine, with `GET /api/v1/workspaces/cloud-accounts` for the connections on offer, and `enable_web_access` only when the agent's own workspace is published and the new one is for the user's own use. Following the old text created a cloud workspace at the connection's default size with its default 50 GB root disk, about 30 GB of it the data volume.

### system

The workspace's mngr moves to the `minds-v0.10.3` release of mngr: the pin in `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` names the public mirror commit of the mngr the 0.10.3 desktop app ships, so a workspace built from this tag runs the same mngr the app drives it with.

The chat-agent-split plan now says a switch keeps listing each held send it has delivered (the record's `delivered_sends`, marked `is_delivered` on the wire) until the switch is done, so the page can show it until its turn reaches the transcript or the agent's queue.

The desktop-interface contracts doc says the roster, the presence listing, and the heartbeat answer from the profile cache (a stale entry included while the workspace is shared), fetch missing or stale profiles in the background, and push `presence_updated` and `roster_updated` again when that changed a profile; that a person nothing names is called `Guest`; that the first start of a shell that keeps desktop owners gives each ownerless desktop `users.json` assigns to a visitor that visitor's key, once, marked by `visitor_desktops_adopted`; and that an arrival seeds a visitor a fresh desktop when the one `users.json` records for them is gone or no longer theirs.

The desktop interface contracts now say the shell announces `reportsChatOnScreen` (embed contract v15) and that a chat's own page sends `minds:chat-on-screen`, which the chat root and the shell forward up unchanged.

mngr is pinned to `44fab61efc`, the public mirror of mngr main with the studio-create-skill change merged. In it Imbue Studio's `GET /api/v1/workspaces` reports each workspace's `launch_mode`, `instance_type` and recorded size, and a new `GET /api/v1/workspaces/cloud-accounts` lists the cloud connections a create may target; the vendored `imbue-studio` skill is re-vendored from that commit and reads both to place a new workspace like the one its agent runs in. Inside the workspace the pin changes only the `minds-workspaces-read` verb's dialog text, which now names those reads.

### system/apps/chat

A message sent while a chat switches provider no longer disappears from the page while the switch delivers it. The switch took each held message off its list as it handed it to the new agent, a few seconds before its turn reached the transcript, so for that moment only the "Starting Claude Code…" line was left. The chat app now keeps listing a delivered message (the switch record's new `delivered_sends`, each marked `is_delivered` on the wire) until the switch is done, and the page shows it until its turn appears in the conversation or the agent's queue, including on a page opened partway through the switch. A message sent again under the same id after the switch delivered it is no longer delivered a second time.

The status row ("Thinking…", a running tool, a switch's "Starting …") now stays under the message that opened the turn it reports, until that message reaches the conversation. It used to jump above the message when the agent started working before the message landed, and above a held message once a switch's marker reached the transcript. A message sent while the agent is already working on an earlier turn still waits below that turn's status row.

- A sender's name in a chat no longer stays stuck on what the page knew when it loaded. When a message arrives naming its author differently than the page's copy of the roster, or naming someone the copy lacks, the page reads the roster again, and an already-drawn message picks up the new name.

- A person nothing names is called "Guest" instead of their account's raw id, both when the chat app names a sender and when the page draws one.

- A failed read of the shell's roster is now logged as a warning (once per run of failures) instead of only at debug level, so a chat that cannot see who is in the workspace is visible in the logs.

A chat's page now tells Imbue Studio when it is really on screen (its window shown and its transcript drawn), so the app can keep its wash over a new workspace until the welcome chat has appeared.

### system/apps/system_interface

- A visitor's desktop made before minds-v0.10.0 is theirs again. Older shells seeded each visitor's desktop with no `owner`, which 0.10.0 reads as the workspace owner's, so after the update a visitor loaded straight into the viewing chrome on their own desktop with nowhere for "Stop viewing" to take them. The shell now gives each ownerless desktop that `users.json` assigns to a visitor that visitor's key on its first start after the update.

- "Stop viewing" no longer does nothing when it finds no other desktop to go to: a toast says the window couldn't leave, because the workspace did not answer or the viewer has no desktop of their own to go to.

- A visitor whose recorded desktop id now names somebody else's desktop (the owner deleted theirs and later made one that took the id) gets a fresh desktop of their own on arrival, with the replaced-desktop notice, instead of landing on the owner's desktop with nowhere to stop viewing to.

- The roster and the presence listing never wait on the connector. Profiles were re-fetched one person at a time inside the request every five minutes, so `GET /api/roster` and the heartbeat could take longer than the chat app's two-second limit. They now answer from the profile cache, a stale entry included, fetch what is missing or stale in the background, and announce the roster and the connected set again when a fetched profile changed.

- A granted person nothing names (no profile name, no email, no arrival yet) is called "Guest" in the roster instead of their account's raw id.

The workspace shell tells Imbue Studio that its chats report themselves on screen, so the app waits for the welcome chat before lifting the wash over a new workspace rather than giving up on it.

### system/libs/workspace_layout

`workspace_layout.roster` gains `UNNAMED_PERSON_DISPLAY_NAME` ("Guest"), the name the shell's roster and the chat app give a person nothing names, in place of their account's raw id.

### system/libs/workspace_ui

`announceReadyToEmbedder` takes `reportsChatOnScreen`, and the new `reportChatOnScreen` sends `minds:chat-on-screen` (embed contract v15, probed by name so an older vendored snapshot still builds).

## [minds-v0.10.2] - 2026-11-09

### system

The workspace's mngr moves to the `minds-v0.10.2` release of mngr: the pin in `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` names the public mirror commit of the mngr the 0.10.2 desktop app ships, so a workspace built from this tag runs the same mngr the app drives it with. This is the first tag that pins the re-uploaded Fortress x64 asset and carries the Screen service's host-echo fix.

The Screen unit's Fortress pin follows the re-uploaded `fortress-v156-linux-x64.tar.gz` of tiliondev/fortress v156.0.8078.47 (digest `fa56589c...`, the one the release's `SHA256SUMS` lists since 2026-11-09): the upstream maintainer replaced the asset in place, so every image build and first-boot install of the Screen refused it as a SHA256 mismatch. The Chromium binary is unchanged; the launcher no longer offers license activation by default, pins the exact timezone, enables the Web Share feature, drops twelve Microsoft fonts, and adds `chrome_sandbox`. The arm64 asset and its pin are unchanged.

The Screen spec says the service tells its own host changes (the `give`, `reset` and locking it makes through neko's REST API) apart from a human taking an uncontrolled Screen by the event's initiator, neko's `API` session, and only keeps its host record from them.

### system/apps/screen

The Screen no longer re-grants control to a session that has just returned it. neko reports the host changes the service itself makes (give, reset, locking) on the same event socket as a human taking an uncontrolled Screen, and the service read every one as the latter, so a late echo of its own `give` put the previous controller back in charge and the next person's first input was dropped as a non-host's; the service now tells its own changes apart by neko's API session as the event's initiator and only keeps its host record from them. Found by the staging smoke run's template suites, where the drop test's take-and-return left the touch test's first touch on the floor. The human take and return verbs now also answer only once the lease has reached neko, so a session that sends its first input right after another returned control is a request neko grants rather than a non-host's input it drops.

## [minds-v0.10.1] - 2026-11-09

### .agents

The `datalib` skill now installs datalib v0.49.0. An embed uses about 3.6 GB less memory, for about 10% less speed, and the first search by meaning after a start no longer loads every vector while you wait. A source that reads local files scans its folder without reading any file. Slack can mirror only the channels that involve the user, and reading a channel clears its unread markers on the next sync. A download interrupted by a lost network now ends incomplete rather than succeeded, and a file whose parser panics fails that file rather than the whole sync. An agent reading a raw store directly should note that whether an email, Slack conversation, Signal message or SMS was read now lives only in the store's `read_marks` table, and that the `fsindex` source type is now `file_inventory`.

The `datalib` skill now installs datalib v0.50.0. Notion pages keep text Notion left out in its place, and bookmarks and embeds are real links; pages that gain from this download once more on the next sync. Slack's raw store says when each conversation was last checked, an imported export no longer follows links out of its folder, and `datalib-step help` now leads an agent to the contacts app, where it should propose links rather than call `POST /link`.

The `datalib` skill now installs datalib v0.51.0. Every PDF re-renders once after the upgrade, because a PDF is now measured before it is read, and a crafted one cannot exhaust memory. The installer refuses a download it cannot check against its checksum, datalib's latchkey no longer pings a usage counter, and the time series card can align the starts of several runs.

The `datalib` skill now installs datalib v0.52.0. A search has one merged answer, with `semantic:off` to leave out meaning, and `tab=` and `--tab` are gone. Email keeps previews and a muted mark, Gmail can fetch each label to its own depth, and anything a sync drops now leaves a trail. An email's muted mark moves to `read_marks.muted` the first time this build opens the store.

The build-app scaffolder pins a new app's type-check ratchet to `ty` 0.0.87 (was 0.0.85), the version every committed project now uses, and gives the app's `pyproject.toml` the workspace root's two-week supply-chain cooldown (`[tool.uv] exclude-newer = "14 days"`), since a scaffolded app is a standalone uv project that the root's setting does not reach.

The manage-desktop skill explains that an app can declare several default shortcuts, and that shortcuts of an app a release retired are removed from every desktop.

`build-app` now shows a new app inside a labeled frame for as long as it is a mock, so the user never mistakes hard-coded content or a sample of their data for the finished app. The frame is the preview wrapper with a "UI Sketch" banner ("early UI sketch -- not the finished app") and a note under it, written by the agent, saying what is not real yet ("Showing 20 of your emails as a sample; refresh doesn't work yet."). It stays up after the user confirms the mock and comes down only once the app reads its real data source: a `fetch-process-show` surface rendering the confirmed `sample.json` is still framed until it is pointed at the pipeline's output.

`build_app_skill/mock_frame.py up --app <name> --note "..." --open|--refresh` frames the app's live program as the `<name>-sketch` app ("<display name> (UI sketch)"), booting nothing else, and re-registers the app itself as internal (out of the launcher) and exempt from the no-window stop (only the frame has a window). The frame records its note and page, so `mock_frame.py refresh --app <name>` needs nothing else: while a frame is up it re-frames the app as recorded and reloads the mock window, which is what puts the hidden registration back after the app restarts (`verify_app.py --restart ... && mock_frame.py refresh`) or the workspace reboots; with no frame up it reloads the app's own windows. `up` without `--note` keeps the current note, and re-framing reuses the wrapper's port, so an open mock window keeps its origin. `mock_frame.py down --app <name>` closes the mock window, removes the frame, and restores the app's registration. `crystallize-creation`, `heal-creation`, and `update-creation` reload an app `build-app` made with `mock_frame.py refresh`, and `update-app` does so while the app is still framed.

`preview_wrapper_server.py` takes `--kind change|mock` (default `change`, the existing preview banner; `mock` is the "UI Sketch" banner) and `--note`. `serve_isolated_instance.py` gains `frame()`, the wrapper boot and registration around a service something else runs, which `down` tears down like any instance, and `read_frame()`, what a frame was booted with.

The `connect-external-service` skill now routes an MCP server through latchkey instead of through the workspace's own MCP client or a harness's MCP config.

A hosted server is a custom latchkey service: its OAuth sign-in goes through latchkey's new `mcp` login flow (sent as the `login` object of a `custom-service` permission request: the authorization endpoint as the login URL, and the MCP endpoint plus the token and registration endpoints its `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` publishes as the parameters), and a server that takes a key in a header is an ordinary custom service on the endpoint's domain. Either way the credential stays in Imbue Studio's credential store, the gateway attaches it and refreshes the token, and the connection is there for every chat, app and scheduled job. The server is then called as a JSON-RPC API through `latchkey curl`, the way latchkey's builtin `*-mcp` services already are. The scopes are fixed at sign-in and nothing adds one later, so the agent asks for broad scopes up front; a scope found missing afterwards means asking the user to disconnect the service and setting it up again.

A server published as a package to run in the workspace is no longer a way to reach a service: it only calls the service's API with a key, so the skill sends the agent to that API (a custom latchkey service, or the direct API with a key from the secret card) instead of running a stranger's code with the workspace's access. With that, `mcpc`, `mcp-servers.json` and `mcpc login` are gone from the skills' guidance; the `use-template` skill treats an `mcp-servers.json` in an older template as a list of connections to request through latchkey.

The template no longer installs `mcpc` or links its store into `data/.secrets/`: the install in `setup_system.sh`, the `1300-mcpc-home-link.sh` env.d unit, and its lines in the seeder and the offload manifests are gone. An existing workspace keeps the mcpc it has (an update re-runs the setup script but uninstalls nothing, and the environment record replays it onto a fresh rootfs), so a connection it made through mcpc keeps working. The secrets guard still treats `~/.mcpc` as a name for the directory, since such a workspace's store stays there, and the template manifests still read an `mcp-servers.json` so an older published template adopts and an older workspace publishes as before.

The skill's routing table now puts the service's own MCP server (row 2) ahead of a custom latchkey service with a pasted key (row 3), since a working MCP sign-in asks the user for one sign-in and no copying. The row is taken only when the server's OAuth metadata publishes a `registration_endpoint`, so latchkey can register itself as a client; a server that needs a hand-registered client, or one that takes a key in a header, falls through to row 3 with the service's API.

`use-ai-integration`'s key snapshot always lands at `/home/user/workspace/data/.secrets/anthropic.env`, whatever directory the writer or a reader runs from. Resolved against the caller's working directory, a run from the skill's or an app's directory wrote the key into a file git sees, and Claude Code records a diff of every git-visible file a Bash command changes, the key's full value included, in the agent's session transcript. `read_workspace_ai_credentials` and `write_anthropic_env_snapshot` also take the snapshot path as an argument, which the tests use instead of changing directory.

The update-self skill's backup precondition documents `host-backup-now --check`'s new exit 4 (the account is out of backup storage, so the newest tick freed space instead of backing up) as one more outcome without a confirmed restore point.

A background agent that leaves work running is still counted as working.

mngr grew a state for an agent whose turn has ended while work it kicked off is still running. Two places listed the states they counted as live, so an agent in the new state read as finished:

- When a lead hands work to a background agent and waits for its report, a background agent that ended its turn with something still running counted as gone, so the lead stopped waiting and looked for a report that was not there yet. It now keeps waiting.

- Before the workspace updates itself it pauses the chats that are doing something. One carrying work past its turn now counts as doing something, so it is paused along with the rest.

The build-app skill's escape hatch says that a wrapped third-party server's window records only that somebody clicked into it, never that they kept using it, and that giving its pages the contract script (the steps it already gives) also makes them report their input like a scaffolded app's.

The build-app scaffold's standalone-project test stages `system/libs/workspace_layout` in full beside the other libraries a scaffolded app installs, since `app-schema` now depends on it and uv builds it from the staged tree.

- `update-self`'s migration reference has a new "Launches and import-path edits in the user's code" section: the update fixes the workspace's own launches and import-path edits that fail the launch rules by restructuring them, never by editing the test, even when that reaches code the update did not otherwise touch.

- `running-python.md` documents the `# own-process:` and `# import-path:` markers for a launch or import-path edit that really has to stay, with a why that says why the site has to stay: for a process or an `other-tree` edit, what an import would break or could not do; for bare code, the stdlib-only packages it imports; for code that must run with no venv whatever it imports, what runs it and why no venv is usable there. Its bare-tier description now counts the libraries on the bare search paths as standard library there and states the cases in which code must run with no venv whatever it imports, and it adds that a deadline is a reason for a process only when the work can hang where no timeout reaches. The built-in skills' own sites that need one carry these markers: the secrets and OOM-band wrappers, the preview server, update-self's calls into the workspace tree or the venv tier, the `sys.path` edits of the bare modules and of the stubs run under the system `python3` or `uv run --no-project`, and update-self's load of the target release's OOM bands.

- An isolated instance of a standalone project (`serve_isolated_instance.py up --project`, and previews of user apps) links the project's venv in-process before each boot and refresh, instead of running `venv_links.py` at the head of the instance's command. A refresh whose link fails leaves the running instance as it was. The scaffold, previews and isolated instances import `forward_port` from `app_registration`.

- `user-package-migration migrate` gives a package whose tests type-check it (`check_no_type_errors`) the root's `ty` pin in its dev group and a `[tool.ty]` table, as build-app's scaffold does. Without them, a migrated app's type check walked up to the root project and failed on every built-in skill's imports. The dev group it writes or adds to lists one requirement per line, and an existing one-line group keeps its items and its comment. Every package it migrates also gets the root's dependency cooldown (`[tool.uv] exclude-newer`), which a standalone project does not inherit, unless it sets its own.

- Every documented wait through `run_in_background.py` (`create_worker.py await` in launch-task, update-self, crystallize-creation, fetch-process-show, heal-creation, update-creation, migrate-workspace, publish-template and the lead-proxy reference; the GitHub-approval waits; datalib's sync wait) passes the new `--waiter` flag.

Testing branch merging `mngr/avoid-api-key-limits` (the `update-self` and `migrate-workspace` skills describe the backup store's `rest:` repositories) and `mngr/remote-execution` (the `run-on-users-computer` skill, the `file-sharing` cross-reference, and the AGENTS.md pointer) so both can be exercised together with their mngr counterparts; the skill changes are the two branches' own, see their entries.

The `run-on-users-computer` skill now triggers only on an explicit request to run something on the user's own physical computer ("on my laptop", "on my local machine", "not in the workspace"). Its opening section says that everything else runs in the workspace, and that a bare "my computer", "my machine", or "my desktop" means the workspace, which is also a computer and the one the user is looking at.

`serve_isolated_instance.py --copy` now checks a copy against what the workspace can actually still write (the `disk_headroom` library, which also reads a cloud machine's disk quota) and keeps 2 GiB of that free, instead of keeping 6 GiB of `statfs` free space to cover a quota it could not see. App previews no longer fail on a machine whose disk shows 4-6 GB free with room to spare, and still refuse when the quota is what is nearly full.

`serve_isolated_instance.py` moves to the venv tier, since it now imports a venv-tier library: run it with `uv run --no-sync`, not `python3` (update-app's commands and the script's own printed hints say so). `running-python.md` says which bare code has to stay bare, and that other stdlib-only code moves to the venv tier when it needs something not already bare.

The caretaker and update-app skills check disk space with `uv run --no-sync disk-headroom` instead of `df`.

Add the `run-on-users-computer` skill: when a task would run a command on the
user's own computer, it says what to try first (file sharing and synced
folders, connected services, computing the result here), that a one-off script
the user runs themselves is fine, and that Imbue Studio's remote-execution
route is the only sanctioned way for an agent to run something there itself,
behind the user's own switch and a per-workspace approval. It tells the agent
to ask for the narrowest program that does the job (a bare name, or a path it
already knows such as a script it wrote under `~/.studio/custom-scripts/`)
rather than for any command, and that a shell or language runtime counts as
any command. It forbids leaving any standing way in (a daemon, a cron entry, a
listener, a tunnel, a polling script). AGENTS.md and the `file-sharing` skill
point at it, and the chat's permission card titles a remote-execution request
"This computer".

An update no longer treats the main chat as something it can pause or stop for memory. The chat app starts the main chat again as soon as it stops, so pausing it never held: the update recorded it as paused while it was already back, and a run freeing memory could keep stopping it without gaining anything. `run-status stop-chats --agent` now refuses the main chat and says why. Before the apply, a busy main chat is still stopped, which interrupts its work, but it is recorded as interrupted: the resume sends it the note without trying to start it. The update and memory guides say the main chat cannot be stopped for memory.

### system

The shared frontend library (`system/libs/workspace_ui`) drops its `--width-agent-gutter` variable from `base.css`. Its one user, the chat transcript, now caps the agent's bubbles and tool-call rows itself, so nothing reads the variable.

`uv.lock` and the root project record `ty` 0.0.87 (was 0.0.85) for every project's type-check ratchet.

The root `pyproject.toml` carries the same two-week supply-chain cooldown as mngr-internal: `[tool.uv] exclude-newer = "14 days"`, so a relock only adopts a registry release once it has been public for two weeks, with `required-version = ">=0.10"` because an older uv drops a relative cutoff silently. The lock records the window (`exclude-newer-span = "P14D"`), and `types-pyyaml` moves back from 6.0.12.20261030 to 6.0.12.20260906, the newest release the window admits.

`system/libs/workspace_voice/` is a new member of the npm workspace (and the image copies its manifest): dictation for the workspace's pages, which the chat's composer now offers (see the chat's and the library's own entries). The desktop interface's and the workspace app model's contracts document the field, the `app` object, and the registry key; `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` names the speech model and the speech detector dictation downloads and ships.

A new guard, `agent_block_foreground_sleep.sh`, blocks any command that waits on a foreground `sleep` of 5 seconds or more, on every harness (claude, codex, pi and agy). Agents had been starting their tests in the background and then polling the output on a guessed schedule (`sleep 240; cat <output>`), holding their turn for minutes after the tests had finished, with messages to them queued until the sleep ended. The refusal tells the agent to wait on the event instead: run the command through `run_in_background.py` (or the harness's own background option) and end the turn, or check the state it is waiting for with short sleeps (`until curl -sf <url>; do sleep 1; done`). Sleeps under 5 seconds, a sleep in a list sent to the background with `&` (such as the `mcpc login` sign-in in `connect-external-service`), a sleep inside the command handed to `run_in_background.py`, and a claude call made with `run_in_background` are allowed. `AGENTS.md` gains the same rule as prose, including when a timed wait is legitimate (the user asked to check back later, a retry-after, pacing a rate-limited API) and that it then goes in a background command. The tool-call policy contract records it as P11. The pipe-into-`head`/`tail` guard now finds a stage's command the same way the sleep guard does, so it also sees past a leading `elif` or `{`.

The desktop-interface contract and plan, the launcher, post-launch-paths and phone plans, the Screen spec, and the window-bound-resources spec describe an app's several default shortcuts (`default_shortcut` as one table or an array, `default_shortcuts` on the registry entry), the removal of shortcuts of an app no longer registered, `default_shortcuts_offered.json` version 2 (the offered `(app, launch)` targets, with version 1 read as each app's first), and a focus shortcut of a one-window app's POST launch path always launching.

`forward_port.register_manifest(path, manifest_path, url, overrides=...)` registers an app from its manifest, as `--manifest` does, with its `internal` and `stop_when_no_windows` replaced on the row until the next plain registration. `build-app`'s mock frame uses it to hide the app it frames and keep it running while only the frame has a window.

The desktop-interface docs describe how the shell now hides pages: hidden and fully covered pages are parked out of the viewport rather than set to `display: none`, a covered page stays shown to the app contract, and the shell answers a hidden page's `shell:capabilities` with `shell:hidden`. The window radius token is now one of the metrics the shell reads, so it must be a pixel length.

Bump Latchkey version to 3.22.1.

CI pins its two non-GitHub actions to full commit SHAs, with the ref each corresponds to in a trailing comment: `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` (its `stable` branch as of 2026-10-16) and `imbue-ai/use-vault-secrets` (its `main` as of 2026-10-21). A moved branch on either repository can no longer change the code that runs in the job holding the Modal token from Vault. GitHub's own `actions/*` stay on their major-version tags, and `astral-sh/setup-uv` was already pinned.

The desktop interface contract (`docs/system/blueprint/desktop-interface/contracts.md`, section 4.3) records `clients.json` version 3: a version-2 file is read with every client's pinned entries in the taskbar with no floating position, and rewritten at version 3 on the next write.

`docs/system/analytics-collection.md` names the two feeds this template's own services write for the explorer analytics collection, the share gateway's per-minute request counts and the shell's `window_opened` client-activity events, and says the gateway's per-request access log is never collected. The root workspace gains the `event_streams` library as a member.

`provision_backups.py` (the hosted web client's in-workspace `restic init`) no longer retries through credential propagation: the backup store's tokens are valid the moment they are issued, so a refusal is reported at once.

The workspace's mngr moves to the `minds-v0.10.1` release of mngr: the pin in `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` names the public mirror commit of the mngr the 0.10.1 desktop app ships, so a workspace built from this tag runs the same mngr the app drives it with.

`docs/specs/chat-send-failure-system.md` covers the send ledger's part in Retry: Retry goes under the failed send's send-time id, so the chat app answers it as it answered that send when the send was taken after all, and a send that got no answer is handled as `submission_unconfirmed`.

`docs/specs/chat-send-failure-system.md` and `docs/specs/send-failure-notice.md` now describe the notice's own sentence for each kind of send failure, the Restart button, a stopped send answering `withdrawn`, and the chat app keeping the sends behind "Sent again".

mngr is pinned to the paired mngr change, whose Claude terminal reader no longer streams Claude's own status lines (a finished tool group's "Ran 3 shell commands" summary, a running tool's blinking marker, the "main" row of the background-agents list) as part of a reply.

`docs/system/analytics-collection.md` and the desktop-interface contract name the shell's `window_input` client-activity events: the heartbeat's `client_id` and `input_windows` fields (section 5.1), the event's shape and once-per-minute rule, and the client-activity log's archive rule (section 6).

The Fortress env.d unit (`system/scripts/env.d/2000-screen.sh`) installs a second managed Chromium policy, `deny-local-network-access.json`, setting `LocalNetworkAccessBlockedForUrls` to every URL: the browser on the Screen gates a public page's requests to loopback behind a permission prompt, and the policy answers that prompt for the user, so no page the browser shows can ask to reach the workspace's loopback services (imbue-ai/mngr-internal#2816). A page on loopback reaching loopback is not a local network request and is untouched. The two policy installers share one `_install_policy_file`, and `fortress_distrust_policy_test.py` is now `fortress_policies_test.py`, covering both.
