- `system/test_python_launch_rules.py` no longer counts launches of the workspace's own code or edits to the import path: each one fails unless a marker in the comment lines above its statement (`# own-process: <reason> -- <why>`, `# import-path: <reason> -- <why>`) names one of the reasons `running-python.md` gives. A marked `sys.path` edit may add a directory outside the bare search paths, except in code the system `python3` runs, where only an `other-tree` edit may. A marker with an unknown reason, no why, or no site below it fails. Both failure messages give the usual fix and the marker format, and give the agent leave to restructure the code involved. Every template site either became an import or carries a marker, and the test's own list of `sys.path` exceptions is gone.

- The import-path check also reads `PYTHONPATH=` in tracked shell scripts. The launch scan no longer flags a path that is only written, read or checked (as `scaffold_skill.py` writes a new skill's `run.py`, which flagged any workspace with exactly one crystallized skill), a console-script name that is an argument rather than the program an argv runs (`supervisorctl status env-converge`), a list or tuple holding another (a route table's row), or a file naming its own path.

- `forward_port` moved from `workspace_bare_scripts` into the new stdlib-only `system/libs/app_registration` library, which is on the bare search paths. `system/scripts/forward_port.py` runs it as before.

- `run_in_background.py --waiter`, for a command that only waits and is safe to start over: it runs in the runner's OOM band (200) instead of the caller's 900, so a lead's wait on its worker is no longer shed with the worker's test runs. If a signal ends it anyway while the caller's agent still has live processes, the runner starts it again, up to three times, and notes each restart in the output.

Testing branch merging `mngr/avoid-api-key-limits` (the backup store: `provision_backups.py` drops its credential-propagation retry) and `mngr/remote-execution` (the `run-on-users-computer` skill, pointed at from AGENTS.md) so both can be deployed and exercised together with their mngr counterparts (imbue-ai/mngr-internal#2854). mngr is pinned to the public export of that merged mngr branch.

AGENTS.md's pointer at the `run-on-users-computer` skill now says commands run in the workspace by default, and that the skill is for an explicit request to run something on the user's own physical computer.

The desktop-interface contract (`docs/system/blueprint/desktop-interface/contracts.md`, section 5.1) records what the roster now lists and carries (the mngr repo's `specs/multiplayer-refinements/spec.md`, section 4.2, and mngr-internal issue #2732): the display order places every account a workspace-level domain grant admitted (the presence records whose email's domain the grants still name) after the accounts the grants name and before the invited emails; each participant carries `is_admitted_by_domain`; and a person's name falls back, after their profile and their arrival record, to what the Imbue Studio desktop recorded of the account in `data/.secrets/share_identities.json` (`{"version": 1, "identities": {"<user_id>": {"email", "display_name"}}}`, written beside the grants with every save), before their email's local part and their id.

A workspace container that docker restarted on its own (an out-of-memory kill of the gVisor sandbox, a docker daemon restart, a VM reboot) came back with nothing in it but sshd until the Imbue Studio desktop app happened to notice: the services agent, supervisord, and every service, the share gateway included, stayed down (the 2026-11-08 world-builder outage). The image now installs `/usr/local/bin/mngr-container-start-hook` (`system/scripts/minds_container_start_hook.sh`), which mngr's container entrypoint runs on every start: when the services agent already exists (a restart docker made on its own, or a start of a stopped workspace) it records a `container_restarted` event in the agent's `events/host_lifecycle/events.jsonl` (`workspace_bare_scripts/record_container_restart.py`) and relaunches the agent through the shared start script; on the container's first start it does nothing.

earlyoom's README and configuration record that a cloud workspace's VM now publishes `/mngr-vol/.host-meminfo` too (mngr_vps), so earlyoom sees the cgroup's real headroom under gVisor on AWS, GCP, Azure, Vultr, and OVH as it already did on Imbue Cloud slices.

The `disk-headroom` command joins the root project's dependencies so its console script survives a sync of the root closure, and bug reports record the cloud machine's published disk quota (`/mngr-vol/.host-diskinfo`) beside `df -h`. The System Monitor spec describes the disk view's figures as the workspace can use them.

mngr is pinned to the public export of mngr-internal#2791 (branch `mngr/remote-execution`), the paired mngr change. That change lives in what Imbue Studio's desktop app runs, not in the workspace: the desktop gateway's `permission-requests` extension accepts the `remote-execution` request type the `run-on-users-computer` skill files, and the app gains the "This computer" switch and approval dialog behind it, so a workspace needs an updated Imbue Studio, not this pin, to use the route. Of the packages a workspace installs from the pin only `concurrency-group` changes, with an option nothing here uses. The pin pairs the two branches so the template's CI and the paired-branch harnesses build workspaces against that mngr; once the mngr PR merges, the twice-daily bump moves the pin to the mirror of mngr `main`.

The System Monitor spec's disk breakdown table (`docs/system/specs/system-monitor.md` section 4.4) lists `/var/cache/user` among the package caches, less the venvs beside the uv cache, and leaves it out of the system software, which counts the venvs, adds a "Chats, logs and settings" row for the home folder less the workspace and the caches, and says when "Everything else" lists the system software and the rest of the disk.

The workspace contracts doc says the chat pages' `provisional_chat_created` message carries the chat's held sends as the page draws them: the words without the author prefix, and who sent them.

### system/apps/chat

The agent's side of the chat follows the multiplayer-chat prototype.

- The agent's name and face show once per stretch of its output, which runs until a person speaks or another agent takes over. Before, they repeated over every bubble that followed a tool call.

- Each message's prose is a bubble. A turn's closing reply below its steps is now a bubble too, not plain text.

- Tool calls, the step timeline and system notices sit between the bubbles on their text edge, 12px apart. A thin line runs through their icons, bullets and ticks.

- The call the agent is running shows in its own chip on the line, with the working dot and the turn's clock, in place of the status line. A call inside a step's work is said by the status line, which joins the line as the stretch's last piece. The done mark is a small receipt just under the stretch.

- "You" shows over the first of a run of your own messages. Another person's name and picture show once per run of theirs.

- A command you run in bash mode (`!ls`) and its output stand on your side and end the agent's stretch, as a new `person_chip` display kind.

- The chevron beside the step the agent is working on no longer draws doubled once that step is opened: the title's shimmer now sweeps only its words.

The type-check ratchet runs `ty` 0.0.87 (was 0.0.85). 0.0.87 rejects a request handler that re-declares the `server` attribute it inherits with a narrower type, and its two findings are fixed: the stand-in sign-in CLI's callback handler remembers the outcome of its one callback itself, so it no longer needs a server subclass to write it to, and the sign-in relay tests' listener checks the server's type where it reads the port instead of re-declaring the attribute.

The composer dictates. A mic button sits left of Send (and Cmd+Shift+M, or Ctrl+Shift+M off a Mac, works anywhere in the chat page): speech is turned into text on the user's own device, by a model the page downloads from Hugging Face at a pinned commit and runs in a worker every chat page of the workspace shares, so the workspace itself pays no memory for voice (the workspace-voice-input spec in the mngr repository). Dictated words land at the caret, fitted to the sentence around them; unfinished words are rewritten in place until they are final, and only final words are saved to the draft. The box is read-only while listening, and the mic's capsule fills with the input level, in the neutral pressed tint. Enter or Send while dictating finishes the words first, then sends; Escape drops the words that are not yet final. Dictation has no length limit. The speech model's download shows as a ring on the mic with its progress in the tooltip; a problem (a blocked, missing, or busy microphone, a failed download, words that could not be transcribed) shows in a notice over the composer, with Retry where it can help. Hiding the page stops dictation and keeps its words; closing it drops the unfinished ones; a dictation started in another chat of the workspace stops this one.

The chat page's Content-Security-Policy gains `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` in `script-src`, which compiling the speech model's WebAssembly needs and which admits nothing else, and Hugging Face's hosts (`https://huggingface.co` and `https://*.hf.co`) in `connect-src`, for the model's download. The manifest declares `uses_microphone = true`, so the shell hands the microphone to the chat's frames, and the chat root's inner frames allow it too.

The tool-call policy contract (`harnesses/core-contracts/tool-call-policies.md`) gains P11: a command must not wait on a foreground `sleep` of 5 seconds or more. The state-of-things file records it as live on claude, codex, pi and agy.

The chat app's test registry row writes its default shortcut as `default_shortcuts`, the registry key the shell reads now. No change to the app itself.

The minimized-chat e2e test follows the shell's new way of hiding pages: a minimized chat keeps its real size while hidden, so the test checks that it stays at its place without waiting for the page to collapse to zero height.

Do not use `mcpc` any more.

Scrolling to the bottom of a chat while the agent is writing stays at the bottom. Before, the view could jump back up about a message's height just as it got there and then slide back down, so it looked like the wheel couldn't quite reach the end.

- Typing a long message no longer makes the transcript jump up a line each time the text wraps. When the message box grows, the transcript re-pins to its bottom before the screen redraws, not a frame later.

- Once a message outgrows the message box, the line being typed stays fully in view instead of sitting partly under the box's bottom edge.

A message whose send got no answer from the chat app is no longer reported as failed while it may have arrived, or delivered twice.

- A message whose send got no answer from the chat app (the connection dropped, or a proxy gave up on a long send) is no longer reported as failed while it may have been delivered. The page sends it again under the same send-time id for about half a minute, and the chat app answers a repeat as it answered the first send, a refusal included, waiting for it while it is still under way, instead of delivering it twice. If it still gets no answer, it gets the unconfirmed notice ("Couldn't confirm your message arrived", Send again, no Force), and its copy goes back in the composer and comes back out once the agent's turn for it shows up. Retry after a failed send goes under the failed send's id the same way.

A message is no longer lost or shown twice when the chat's sign-in fails.

- When a chat's login expires and the user signs that account in again, the chat sends again, on its own, the message the expired login refused, once the sign-in has restarted the agent. Every live chat on that account whose last reply was the sign-in error does this, wherever the sign-in finished. While it happens, the failed turn reads "Signed in again. Sending your message again…". Nothing is sent again for a turn the agent had already started working on, when the user has written since, or while the chat is switching to another provider.

- When the chat cannot send it on its own (the chat was stopped, its restart or the resend failed), the failed turn reads "Signed in again." and offers "Send your message again" while it is still the chat's newest turn. When a resend of several refused messages stops partway, the ones it did not get to stay offered. The provider's original text stays under "See details". Each account now records when it last finished a sign-in, and `GET /api/accounts` carries it as `signed_in_at`.

- "Send your message again" under a sign-in error handles a send as the composer does: one the chat app delivered by sending it twice shows "Sent again" under the message, one that cannot be confirmed or gets no answer says so and offers Send again in place of Try again, and every press sends the message under the id its first press used.

- Once a refused message is sent again right after its sign-in error, by the chat, by the button, or typed again by hand before anything else, the original message and its sign-in error are hidden, so the message shows once, whichever order the agent wrote the error and the message in. The same words written after some other message are a new message, and hide nothing. This replaces the rule that hid every sign-in error from before the chat's first reply: such an error now stays when the user wrote something else next.

The failure notice for a send now says what happened in the chat's own words for each kind of failure, rather than showing mngr's reason, and the Force button is now Restart. An unclassified failure still shows the reason, the only account of what went wrong.

Stopping an agent while a message is still being sent to it no longer leaves two copies in the composer and a failure notice: the message comes back once.

The chat app's log now records each failed send's kind and each message it sent again.

"Sent again" now comes from the chat app rather than the page that sent the message, so it shows in every window and after a reload. It also covers a message held through a chat switch and an Antigravity block that lands on a later pass, which showed nothing before. The chat app forgets these when it restarts.

A reply the agent is still writing now shows where its words will land. While a step is open, the text streams in as that step's caption (or at the end of its work, when the step is expanded), the way it reads once it lands, rather than at the bottom of the chat outside the step. With no step open it shows below the chat as before.

A Claude agent's streamed reply no longer repeats text the chat already shows. Once a run of tool calls finished, Claude's terminal summarizes them as "Ran 4 shell commands" under the text before them, and that summary was read as part of a new reply, so the earlier text showed a second time with the summary attached. While a background helper agent ran, the "main" row of Claude's agent list could also show as a reply. Both come from the mngr Claude plugin's terminal reader, fixed in the mngr commit this template now pins.

A step the agent left open at the end of one turn no longer swallows its answer to your next message, or the answer of the agent you switch the chat to. What the agent says goes to the normal reply until it works on that step again, and a turn that never returns to the step does not show it again, so a quick follow-up question is answered as a reply rather than as a caption under an unrelated, still-spinning step.

A chat whose agent is working on something it started no longer reads as stopped.

mngr grew a state for an agent whose turn has ended while work it kicked off is still running -- a background command, a helper agent, a watcher -- so the next thing to move the chat is that work rather than you. The chat app decided whether an agent was alive by listing the states it recognised as alive, and a state missing from that list reads as dead: such a chat showed as stopped, its row hid the work, a plain turn ending dropped its archived members, and a timer would have restarted an agent that was busy.

Alive and "has a turn in flight" are now separate questions. A chat carrying work past its turn is alive, but no turn is open, so the live-turn reading it feeds is unchanged.

Its row also shows as working on something again for the kinds of task this workspace keeps no record of its own for -- a tool call out to another service, a teammate, a cloud session -- which mngr reports and the markers here do not. A turn in progress or a permission request still takes precedence over it.

Only chats created after this reaches the workspace report the new state: mngr writes what an agent needs to report it into the agent's own area when the agent is made, so a chat that already exists keeps running what it was made with, and a new turn does not change that. Those chats behave exactly as they did before, and the workspace's own record of background tasks is what keeps them showing as working.

The chat app's memory prioritizer no longer re-tags every chat on the request thread of every presence heartbeat, send and lifecycle change. A heartbeat that leaves a chat as open and as visible as it was asks for nothing; an event that does change something only asks the prioritizer's one background thread for a pass, which runs at most one pass every two seconds and reads the pid registry once for all chats instead of once per chat. Previously each event ran a full pass, scanning the registry and `/proc` once per chat, with no limit on how many ran at once, so a shared workspace with dozens of open chats could pile up request threads until the chat service stopped answering. A chat's band is now written a moment after the request returns, and a pass that takes more than five seconds logs a warning.

The chat app installs the request guard ahead of its routes (`app_schema.request_guard`): a request the workspace's own browser marks as a page of another origin's is refused with 403, and a request with no `X-Imbue-Identity` header reads as the owner's only from loopback under a loopback `Host`, so a page shown on the Screen's browser can no longer send a chat's agent a message as the owner (imbue-ai/mngr-internal#2816). In-workspace scripts and the shell are unaffected.

- `test_a_watcher_released_before_it_starts_leaves_no_watch_thread_running` is marked flaky, so offload retries it. It still leaves watcher threads running now and then in CI, after the deflake that targeted it.

Testing branch merging `mngr/avoid-api-key-limits` and `mngr/remote-execution`. For the chat app it carries the "This computer" permission card title unchanged; see the remote-execution branch's entry.

The chat's avatar floats over the windows by default (`default_mode = "floating"` on its pinned entry) instead of sitting docked in the taskbar's tray; a client that already chose a mode keeps it, and the entry menu still moves it either way.

When a chat can't reply because its AI account is signed out (an expired sign-in or a revoked key), the chat now tells the Imbue Studio app. You get a notification (the bell, a toast, and a system banner when you're looking elsewhere), and clicking it opens the chat, where the reply has the sign-in button. A chat that keeps failing sends one notification, not one per message, until a reply goes through again. If you're already looking at the chat, nothing pops up.

The permission card titles a `remote-execution` request "This computer", the name Imbue Studio's own request dialog and Settings section use for the user's computer, instead of falling back to the raw request type.

ChatGPT's browser sign-in no longer tells you to turn on "Enable device code sign-in" in ChatGPT's security settings first: OpenAI removed that setting, and code sign-in now works for personal and organization accounts without it. A code sign-in that cannot start says so and suggests trying again or using an OpenAI API key, instead of pointing at the removed setting.

In a shared workspace, a message that has not reached the agent yet is now drawn under its sender, like the turn it becomes. Previously a visitor's queued message showed the raw `[from: <name>]` prefix the agent is handed, in the viewer's own bubble on the right, until the agent took it. Sends held while a chat is still being created showed the prefix the same way, and they and sends held while a chat switches harness or account showed every sender's message as the viewer's own.

The chat snapshot now joins each queued entry and each held send to the chat's author annotations: queued entries the way a transcript turn is joined, held sends by their message id. Each one carries `author` and `author_name`, and a queued entry carries the words behind the prefix as its `display_body`. The provisional chat's `held_sends` are now sent as they render (the words, the display decision and the author) rather than as the stored record. Queued, held and returned-after-a-switch bubbles all draw through the same own-or-other bubble a transcript turn uses.

A message with attached files no longer shows a "See attachment here:" label in its bubble: the images and file links appear on their own under your text. The agent still receives the label with the file paths.

An image you just sent shows in its bubble at once, drawn from the copy already in your browser; each chat keeps up to 25 MB of these copies and loads older ones from the workspace. An image that still has to load holds a box with a faint picture outline and a slow sweep of light, then fades in once it arrives, so a message that is only an image no longer shows as an empty bubble. Images uploaded from now on record their width and height in their stored path, so that box takes the image's own shape and nothing jumps when it loads, on any device; older uploads keep a fixed-shape box. The bubble shown the moment you press send draws its attachments the same way, instead of the raw file-path text. An SVG that declares only its shape (a viewBox) and no size now shows in your bubble instead of an empty one.

### system/apps/screen

The type-check ratchet runs `ty` 0.0.87 (was 0.0.85); the project passes it unchanged.

The Screen declares two default desktop shortcuts, Screen and Browser, so the desktop has the same two entries as the launcher. A workspace that already had the Screen shortcut gets the Browser one added once.

The Screen reads `X-Imbue-Identity` as every app does (`workspace_layout.identity`): a present header that does not parse is refused with 400 rather than read as the owner's, and a session's display name is the email's local part, else Owner or Guest (the `name` an older proxy stamped is no longer read).

The service installs the request guard ahead of its routes (`app_schema.request_guard`): a request the browser on the Screen marks as a page of another origin's is refused with 403 whatever it carries, and a header-less request counts as the owner's only from loopback under a loopback `Host`, so a page shown on the Screen's own browser can no longer drive the owner-only API (`/api/run`, the agent verbs, the screenshot, the browser fleet) over `127.0.0.1:8090` (imbue-ai/mngr-internal#2816). Agents' clients and the shell are unaffected.

Chromium's launch arguments are checked never to disable its Local Network Access checks, the browser-side layer in front of the services' own check.

Copy and paste between your computer and the Screen works again, over a shared link too, and clicking into the Screen no longer pops a "Paste" button (Safari, Firefox) or a clipboard permission prompt (Chrome).

Pasting text copied from a terminal or an editor (which carries an HTML flavor beside the plain text) now lands on the Screen: neko writes one X clipboard target and kept only the HTML when the viewer sent both, so a URL bar or a terminal had nothing to paste. The viewer sends the plain text alone.

A paste no longer comes back as "Copied from the Screen" and overwrites the clipboard on your computer with an HTML rendering of what you pasted. neko reads its own write back with the HTML equal to the text (an `xclip` owner answers every target with its one payload) and announces it like any other change; the viewer now recognises the echo by the plain text, and treats HTML equal to the text as no HTML. Pasting back something copied on the Screen leaves the Screen's clipboard as it was, rich flavors included.

The viewer's calls to neko's routes (the clipboard text and image reads and the text write, the screencast fallback, the logout) carry the session token in the `token` query parameter, as its WebSocket already did, instead of an `Authorization: Bearer` header: the share gateway reads such a header as a visiting agent's admission token and refuses the request, and strips it from what it forwards, so over a share every paste failed with "The text could not be pasted on the Screen" and copying from the Screen failed silently.

The viewer no longer reads the local clipboard when its window gains focus; a paste (Ctrl+V, Cmd+V) is the one way text and images cross to the Screen, and its event carries the data with no permission at all. A paste while this viewer does not hold control says "Take control to paste on the Screen" in the strip instead of vanishing.

### system/apps/system_interface

The type-check ratchet runs `ty` 0.0.87 (was 0.0.85); the project passes it unchanged.

The shell adds `microphone` to the `allow` attribute of the live page frames of an app whose manifest declares `uses_microphone` (the chat, for its composer's dictation), and of no other app's. The inventory's `app` object carries the flag, and the frontend's app record reads it.

Desktop shortcuts of an app that is no longer registered are removed. A workspace updated off the old browser app kept its Browser shortcut on every desktop, and opening it said "browser is not registered". On every read of the desktops the shell now drops the shortcuts of any app the app registry does not list, such as an app a release retired, whose entry the update removed. A registry with no entries drops nothing.

An app can now have several default desktop shortcuts. The Screen gets both a Screen and a Browser shortcut, matching its two launcher entries.

- `default_shortcuts_offered.json` records which `(app, launch)` shortcuts were offered, not which apps (version 2). That way a workspace that already had the Screen shortcut still gets the Browser one. The old list of apps is read as each app's first shortcut and rewritten on the first read.

- The shortcuts that were dropped are cleared from that record, so an app that registers again gets them back. A shortcut the user removed themselves still stays removed.

- The app list in `GET /api/inventory` carries `default_shortcuts` (a list) in place of `default_shortcut`.

- An app's second and later default shortcuts are labeled with their launch path ("Browser"), not the app's name, so the two Screen shortcuts can be told apart.

- Right-clicking any of an app's shortcut entries in the launcher offers to add or remove that shortcut.

- A focus-mode shortcut of a one-window app's POST launch path (the Screen's Browser) always runs it into the app's window, as the launcher's row does, instead of only raising that window, so the Browser shortcut always opens the browser. Other focus shortcuts still just raise the app's last window.

An app that stops when no window shows it now gets the full 60 seconds again each time its program restarts. Before, a restart did not reset the countdown, so an app restarted shortly before its 60 seconds ran out, such as `verify_app.py --restart` during `build-app`, was stopped a few seconds later, while its page was still loading.

The browser no longer renders the pages of windows that are hidden or completely covered by other windows. Covered apps kept rendering at full frame rate, so a busy desktop could hold the renderer above 100% CPU. They also kept their share of the GPU memory all of a workspace's apps share. Past that budget, parts of the desktop went missing on alternate frames, so it flickered during a resize and could keep flickering until the next one.

- A page the windows in front of it completely cover is moved out of the viewport and made invisible, which stops the browser rendering it in Chromium, Safari and Firefox. It is still shown as far as the app is concerned: it gets no `shell:hidden`. Rounded corners are respected, so the notches two snapped windows leave over a third keep that page live. A page whose content is wholly outside the desktop is parked too. The focused window is never parked, a window still sliding into place covers nothing until it lands, one sliding away uncovers at once, and nothing is covered while a window is being dragged or resized.

- Minimized windows and windows on another desktop are hidden the same way instead of with `display: none`. Their apps keep their size and scroll position (`display: none` collapsed them to 0x0 and reset the page's scroll), and Safari now stops rendering them too.

- A hidden page whose contract connects after its load is told `shell:hidden` again, since it missed the one sent at load.

The avatar moves into the taskbar on every screen once, when a workspace takes this update, as the 0.10.0 default intended. Under the older floating default, dragging the avatar saved that screen's whole presentation, the floating mode included, so most workspaces kept a floating avatar after 0.10.0. `clients.json` moves to version 3: reading a version-2 file puts every client's pinned entries in the taskbar and clears their floating positions. Floating the avatar again afterwards sticks.

The shell records every window open in the client-activity log as a `window_opened` event (desktop contracts.md section 6): the client, the desktop, the app, the window id, whether the open minted the window or answered an existing one, and the op requester when an op asked for it. Never the path or the title. The analytics collection of an explorer workspace reads it as the signal that an app was used.

The announcement stream's archive rule (stage an oversized `events.jsonl` aside, gzip it off-thread, keep the newest archives) moved into the shared `event_streams` library, which the share gateway's request counts use too.

The avatar reads as working while an agent finishes something it started in the background.

mngr grew a state for an agent whose turn has ended while work it kicked off is still running. The shell decided whether anyone was working by listing the states it counted as work, so an agent in the new state read as idle and the avatar went quiet while the work was still going.

The shell records a person interacting with a window as a `window_input` client-activity event (desktop contracts.md section 6), one per client, window and minute: the page driver keeps the window each page's `shell:input` report came from and carries the windows on the presence heartbeat (`client_id` and `input_windows`), and the shell writes the event with the desktop's app and desktop. A page that has declared no capabilities (a wrapped third-party server) reports no input, so focus landing in its frame, by a click or a raise, is recorded as a `focus` kind instead. Never the path, the title, the key or the pointer position. A heartbeat is never refused for its input fields; a field off its shape drops the reports and records presence as before.

The client-activity log is now bounded the way the announcement stream is: past 8 MiB it is staged aside before a write and gzipped off-thread, two archives kept; the `context` op and the attribution of an agent's op to a page's last message read the live stream alone.

The shell installs the request guard ahead of its routes (`app_schema.request_guard`): a request the workspace's own browser marks as a page of another origin's is refused with 403, other than a GET or HEAD navigation and the two `_static` modules served to other origins on purpose, and a request with no `X-Imbue-Identity` header reads as the owner's only from loopback under a loopback `Host` (imbue-ai/mngr-internal#2816). A present header that does not parse is now answered with 400 on every route by the same hook.

- The update-self launches in `shell/update_notice.py` carry the `# own-process` markers the launch rules now require: `outlives-caller` for the rollback, which restarts the shell that started it, and `other-tree` for `confirm-last`, which must run the checkout's current update-self rather than a copy the shell imported before the last apply.

The shell's type-check ratchet (`test_no_type_errors`) gets a 120-second timeout of its own instead of the suite's 10-second default: the `ty` run it shells out to takes longer than that on a loaded CI sandbox, which made the test fail on time alone. The default-workspace-template branch merged here is otherwise `mngr/avoid-api-key-limits` plus `mngr/remote-execution` (see their entries); neither touches the shell.

The roster lists everyone a domain grant let in (the mngr repo's `specs/multiplayer-refinements/spec.md`, section 4.2, and mngr-internal issue #2732): a person admitted by a workspace-level `email_domains` entry had no roster entry at all, so the tray never showed them, their desktop read as "Left behind", and no Lounge was made for them. A domain grant names nobody, so the roster now lists every presence record whose email's domain the grants still name, after the accounts the grants name and before the invited emails, marked `is_admitted_by_domain`; a revoked domain takes them off the roster again, presence files and all. The person card says "Here through <domain>" for such an entry.

A granted account that has never arrived is named rather than shown as its raw id: the Imbue Studio desktop writes what it knew of each granted account (the email and display name the grant was resolved from) to `data/.secrets/share_identities.json` beside the grants with every save, and the roster falls back to it after the profile and the arrival record, before the email's local part. The shell watches the file like the grants documents, so a save re-announces the roster.

### system/apps/system_monitor

The type-check ratchet runs `ty` 0.0.87 (was 0.0.85); the project passes it unchanged.

The backup summary has a new `out_of_storage` state, shown as "Out of backup storage", when the newest tick skipped its backup over the account's storage quota or the backup store refused the upload.

The System Monitor installs the request guard ahead of its routes (`app_schema.request_guard`): a request the workspace's own browser marks as a page of another origin's is refused with 403, and a request with no `X-Imbue-Identity` header reads as the owner's only from loopback under a loopback `Host`, so a page shown on the Screen's browser can no longer stop a chat's agent or an app as the owner (imbue-ai/mngr-internal#2816).

Testing branch merging `mngr/avoid-api-key-limits` and `mngr/remote-execution`. For the system monitor it carries the backup summary's `out_of_storage` state unchanged; see the backup-store branch's entry.

The disk view's figures now come from `disk_headroom`, so on a cloud machine free space is what the workspace can actually still write: the smaller of the disk's own free space and the room left under the machine's disk quota, which can run out first. The view's note says so.

The disk breakdown's Package caches row now counts `/var/cache/user`, where the workspace's environment points uv's, npm's and other tools' caches (`XDG_CACHE_HOME`). On docker, modal and imbue_cloud workspaces `~/.cache` is a link to it, which `du` does not follow, so those caches were counted as "System software" instead. The system software figure now leaves them out, and on lima, where the link runs the other way, the caches are still counted once. The venvs that every `.venv` links to, kept beside the uv cache, stay out of Package caches (which says it is safe to clear) and count as system software, along with the packages they hardlink from the cache.

A new "Chats, logs and settings" row holds the home folder beside the workspace's files and the caches (agent records and logs, worktrees, chat history, installed tools), with its largest folders listed. That space used to fall into "Other files on the machine's disk", which now holds only what is outside the workspace and says it cannot be freed from here.

"Everything else" no longer calls the rest of a lima workspace's data disk "System software": when the system software walk is larger than what is left, it sits on another disk, and the row lists nothing under it.

### system/libs/app_manifest

The type-check ratchet runs `ty` 0.0.87 (was 0.0.85); the project passes it unchanged.

The manifest gains `uses_microphone` (bool, default false): whether the app's pages listen to the microphone, which the shell then delegates to their frames and to no other app's. The registry row carries it under the same name. The chat is the one built-in that declares it, for its composer's dictation.

`default_shortcut` in `app.toml` can be one table, as before, or several as `[[default_shortcut]]`. A manifest registration (`system/scripts/forward_port.py --manifest`, and `register_manifest`) copies the manifest's `default_shortcut`, whether one table or an array, onto the registry entry as `default_shortcuts`, and clears an older entry's `default_shortcut` key.

`InventoryApp` (the shell's `app` object) carries `uses_microphone`, whether the shell delegates the microphone to the app's frames; it defaults to false, so an answer from a shell that predates it still parses.

`InventoryApp.default_shortcuts` (a list) replaces `default_shortcut`, and `workspace-layout list` lists each app's `default_shortcuts` (reading a shell that still answers one `default_shortcut` as a list of one).

`workspace_layout.identity` gains the request provenance check every in-workspace service installs ahead of its routes (`describe_provenance_refusal` over a `RequestProvenance`, with `is_loopback_address`, `is_loopback_host` and `is_from_another_origin`): a request a browser marks as a page of another origin's (`Sec-Fetch-Site`, other than a GET or HEAD navigation) is refused whatever it carries, a request a proxy stamped is read by its `X-Imbue-Identity` header, and a header-less request is admitted from loopback alone, under a loopback `Host`. The workspace's own browser (the Screen's Chromium) is on loopback too, so a page it shows could otherwise have reached every service as the owner (imbue-ai/mngr-internal#2816).

- `RosterParticipant` gains `is_admitted_by_domain` (default false): whether a workspace-level domain grant, rather than a grant naming them, is what admits the person; the shell lists such people from their presence records (the mngr repo's `specs/multiplayer-refinements/spec.md`, section 4.2).

### system/libs/workspace_profile

The type-check ratchet runs `ty` 0.0.87 (was 0.0.85); the project passes it unchanged.

### system/libs/workspace_themes

- A theme's `--desk-window-radius` is now a desktop metric the validator checks, like the title bar height: it must be a length in `px`, from 0px to 32px. The shell now reads the window radius to tell which windows other windows cover, and a value in another unit (`0`, `0.5rem`) would have stopped it reading any of the theme's metrics.

### system/libs/workspace_ui

Removed the `--width-agent-gutter` variable: the chat now caps the agent's bubbles and tool-call rows itself, so nothing reads it.

The icon set gains `mic` (Lucide's), with `MIC_CAPSULE_PATH`, the capsule the chat's dictation button also draws filled to the input level, and `iconPaths(name)`, an icon's paths alone for a drawing that frames them itself. `Button` gains `pressed`: the neutral pressed look (the fill-active tint in the text colour), for an on/off control whose "on" should not read as the accent; it wins over `selected`.

`isUnansweredRequest` tells a request that got no answer from the app it was sent to (no HTTP response, or a gateway's 502 or 504 with no detail of the app's own) from one the app answered, so a caller can repeat a request that is safe to repeat.

`describeRequestErrorKind` now returns mngr's `state_unknown`, `agent_not_found` and `not_submitted` kinds rather than reading them as `unknown`.

### system/libs/workspace_voice

New: `workspace_voice`, dictation for the workspace's pages (the workspace-voice-input spec in the mngr repository, implementation step 2). On-device speech recognition behind one engine interface, with Moonshine Base as the first and default engine: an engine registry (`voice_models.json`) pinning every file to a Hugging Face commit with its size and SHA-256; a downloader that checks each file against its pinned size and hash and keeps the checked files in the browser's Cache Storage for the workspace's origin (one variant, checked again on every read, evicted by the browser under storage pressure); an engine worker, one SharedWorker per workspace origin and engine that every chat page shares (a dedicated worker where the browser has none), which picks WebGPU or WebAssembly, transcribes one job at a time, and keeps the engine loaded for as long as a page of the workspace is open; the transformers.js adapter with the runtime's caches off; Silero VAD v5 through vad-web with Sculptor's tuning; Sculptor's streaming turn (commit-and-slice, so dictation has no length limit and each preview costs the same); one inference lane with commits ahead of previews, a failed commit retried twice, and words held for Retry or Discard when it keeps failing; the dictation controller a composer drives; the live span that lands words at the caret, fitted to the sentence around them; and the vite plugin that ships the runtime's WebAssembly, the detector's worklet, and the detector's model with an app's build.

### system/services/caretaker

The type-check ratchet runs `ty` 0.0.87 (was 0.0.85); the project passes it unchanged.

The weekly check's "disk nearly full" finding now reads the disk through `disk-headroom`, so on a cloud machine it also fires when the machine's disk quota, which `df` cannot see, is what is nearly full. Where `disk-headroom` cannot run it falls back to `df`.

### system/services/env_converge

The type-check ratchet runs `ty` 0.0.87 (was 0.0.85); the project passes it unchanged.

- A capture whose `npm ls -g` retry cannot run or times out raises `CaptureCommandError`, like every other probe, instead of a raw `FileNotFoundError` or `TimeoutExpired`, so the backup's in-process capture treats it as a failed capture and still takes its snapshot.

### system/services/host_backup

The type-check ratchet runs `ty` 0.0.87 (was 0.0.85); the project passes it unchanged.

Backups now respect the account's Imbue Cloud storage quota before uploading. When the repository is a `rest:` URL (Imbue Studio's backup store), each tick first asks the store `GET <repository>_usage`; over the soft quota the tick records a new `backup_skipped_over_quota` event (with `used_bytes`, `account_used_bytes`, `quota_bytes`, `hard_limit_bytes`) and runs the retention forget plus `restic prune --max-repack-size <half the headroom>` to free space instead of backing up, until the account is under quota again. A server without the probe, or one that does not answer, means no quota information and the tick proceeds as before.

A backup the store refuses for lack of storage (restic's "507 Insufficient Storage") fails at once and its `restic_backup_failed` event carries `reason = "quota_exceeded"`.

`restic backup` and `restic prune` pin `--pack-size 16`, and `restic prune` accepts a repack bound.

- Before each snapshot, the tick runs env-converge's capture in-process instead of `uv run --no-sync env-converge capture`. Each probe the capture runs keeps its own timeout, and the overall 120 s ceiling is gone. The `env_record_capture_completed` event carries `error_message` in place of `exit_code` and `stderr`.

Testing branch merging `mngr/avoid-api-key-limits` and `mngr/remote-execution`. For host_backup it carries the backup-store branch's storage-quota handling unchanged, beside main's in-process env-converge capture; see that branch's entry.

The backup store's usage probe sends a `User-Agent` of its own (`host-backup/1.0`): Cloudflare answered urllib's default `Python-urllib/3.x` agent with a 403 ahead of the Worker, so every tick logged "The backup store refused the usage probe" and proceeded without quota information, and an over-quota account never took the skip-forget-prune path.

### system/services/oom_priority

The type-check ratchet runs `ty` 0.0.87 (was 0.0.85); the project passes it unchanged.

The README's account of how the chat app's prioritizer re-tags chats now matches the prioritizer: a presence report asks for a pass only when it changes whether the chat is open or showing, passes run one at a time on the prioritizer's own thread at most once every two seconds, and each reads the pid registry once for every chat. The registry's and launch wrapper's docstrings name `live_pids_by_agent_id`, which the prioritizer now reads once for all chats, in place of the per-agent `lookup_pids_by_agent_id`.

- The tagging table in the README lists a command an agent waits on through `run_in_background.py --waiter`. It runs in the user-service band (200) with its runner, and a shed one is started again while its agent runs.

- Each bare-tier script in `bin/` marks its `sys.path` edit with `# import-path: no-venv`, as the launch rules now require, saying why it runs without the venv.

The README records that the memory headroom file earlyoom reads with `--host-meminfo` (`/mngr-vol/.host-meminfo`) is now also published by a cloud workspace's VM (mngr_vps's `mngr-vps-container-meminfo.service`), so earlyoom sees the cgroup's real headroom under gVisor on AWS, GCP, Azure, Vultr, and OVH as it already did on Imbue Cloud slices.

`memory_candidates.py` no longer lists the main chat as an idle chat to stop. The chat app starts the main chat again as soon as it stops, so stopping it frees nothing that lasts. The agents section adds a note naming the main chat instead, so a reader knows why it is missing.

### system/services/share_gateway

The type-check ratchet runs `ty` 0.0.87 (was 0.0.85); the project passes it unchanged.

The share gateway records what the share served (`specs/minds-app-usage-signals/spec.md` in the mngr repo):

- caddy writes a per-request access log to `data/.state/share_gateway/access.log`: the visitor's address, the origin, the method, the path, the status, the size and the duration, with every request header, response header and query string deleted by caddy's log filter (the session cookie, admission tokens, handoff tokens and an app's own credentials all travel there). It rolls at 8 MiB with 4 rolled files kept for at most 30 days.

- The verify handler counts every request it answers, keyed by app, requester kind and id, method class and outcome (allowed, or a denial reason), and a flusher thread writes one record per key per minute to `$MNGR_AGENT_STATE_DIR/events/gateway_requests/events.jsonl` under the standard envelope, which the explorer analytics collection reads. At most 256 keys per minute (the rest fold into one overflow record); the stream archives itself at 32 MiB through the new `event_streams` library.

- The gateway's own werkzeug request line is gone (caddy's log supersedes it); denials are still logged.

The README's note on what the explorer analytics collection reads beside the request counts names the shell's `window_input` client-activity events too.

While the share stack is up the runner rewrites `data/.state/share_gateway/status.json` once a minute, so its `updated_at` tells a reader whether a runner is alive: the Imbue Studio desktop disbelieves an `up` stamped more than five minutes ago, which a container restarted with its services down otherwise left behind as a misleading `up`.

## [minds-v0.10.0] - 2026-11-02

### .agents

- Skill and reference commands run one-offs as `uv run --no-sync ...`, and the new `.agents/shared/references/running-python.md` gives the rule: one-offs use `uv run --no-sync` unless the instruction says `python3`, a long-running process never runs under `uv run`, and a script's top-level imports stay light.

- The github-sync service's program line and the service-processes example run the entry point from `.venv/bin` after a `--frozen` sync instead of under `uv run`.

- update-self advances the environment snapshot with `uv run --no-sync env-converge upgrade` after an apply, and the build-app scaffold validates a new manifest with `uv run --no-sync app-manifest`.

- `running-python.md` describes where the venv is kept current: a `--frozen` sync at boot, at worker provisioning, and at claude and codex session start, none of which rewrites `uv.lock`.

- update-app's preview launches the app from the worktree the way a supervisord program runs: a `--frozen` sync of the worktree's environment, then the app exec'd from its `.venv`, instead of under `uv run`, so the preview never relocks the worktree and no uv process stays resident as its parent. update-app's docs say to run `uv lock` in the worktree before a `refresh` after a dependency change.

Each skill's Python now lives in its own uv project, `.agents/skills/<name>/python/`: a `pyproject.toml` and a `<skill_name>_skill` package, with tests beside the modules. A skill's scripts run from their modules by path, and `scripts/` keeps shell scripts plus an entry stub only where something outside the release runs a fixed path or the script runs with no venv: launch-task's `create_worker.py`, update-self's two and publish-template's two manifest tools, each saying why it stays. `.agents/shared/scripts` is a project too (package `agents_shared`). A script's imports decide how it runs: one that imports only the standard library (and the bare `workspace_bare_scripts`) runs as `python3 <path>`, with no venv; any other runs as `uv run --no-sync <path>`, and its dependencies resolve in the workspace lock. update-self stays on the system `python3` and still stages as one unit; its entry files put the skill's `python/` on `sys.path`.

- **Scripts that call scripts:** the shared preview script registers its servers through `forward_port` in-process and starts the preview frame by its path under its own interpreter; `preview_app.py` boots, refreshes and tears down previews by calling it in-process; launch-task sends the task and every reply through `message_chat` in-process, and a failed task send is reported with the destroy hint instead of raising; build-app's scaffold validates the manifest with `app_manifest` in-process.

- **Third-party skills are left as they came:** a skill installed or copied in from elsewhere is listed in the new `.agents/third-party-skills.toml` with where it came from, and the import-cost and launch checks leave listed skills out; every other skill is held to them. A `scripts/` of plain or PEP 723 scripts never touches the workspace's uv setup. Built-in skills carry `metadata.author: imbue` (`datalib` and `imbue-studio` now do too).

- **What existing workspaces need:** a workspace's own skills with Python need the same layout. The update worker converts them by following the new `update-self/references/python-packaging-migration.md`, which also covers a skill test that loads its module from a file: it imports the module from the package instead. When a check fails on a skill, the worker first decides from the skill's history, its files and the chat that added it whether the workspace made it, and lists one that came from elsewhere instead of converting it. `migrate-workspace` converts the skills it brings over from an older workspace the same way, and carries over the old workspace's third-party list when it has one.

- **Commands that changed:**
  - `notify_user.py`, `request_secret.py`, `serve_isolated_instance.py`, `resolve_template_base.py` and the preview wrapper import only the standard library, so they run from their modules under `python3`: `.agents/skills/notify-user/python/notify_user_skill/notify_user.py`, `.agents/skills/connect-external-service/python/connect_external_service_skill/request_secret.py`, and `.agents/shared/scripts/agents_shared/` for the rest. The chat's secret card and the secret guards still recognise `request_secret.py` at its new path.
  - `preview_app.py` and `parse_task_frontmatter.py` run from their modules with `uv run --no-sync`: `.agents/skills/update-app/python/update_app_skill/preview_app.py` and `.agents/shared/scripts/agents_shared/parse_task_frontmatter.py`.
  - `refresh_workspace_view.py` and `verify_app.py` (now `system/scripts/workspace_scripts/verify_app.py`) are run with `uv run --no-sync` instead of `python3`.
  - `claude_p.py` lives at `python/use_ai_integration_skill/claude_p.py`.
  - update-self's apply refreshes the open views with `uv run --no-sync`.
  - These run from their modules with `uv run --no-sync`: `.agents/shared/scripts/agents_shared/validate_skill.py`, `.agents/skills/build-app/python/build_app_skill/scaffold_flask_lib.py` and `.agents/skills/migrate-workspace/python/migrate_workspace_skill/migrate_workspace.py`.
  - `datalib`'s `sync_request.py` runs from its module, `.agents/skills/datalib/python/datalib_skill/sync_request.py`, with `uv run --no-sync` instead of `python3`.

- **Bare skills:** a skill whose Python is one script that imports only the standard library can stay a single file, `scripts/<name_with_underscores>.py` (its test, if any, beside it as `scripts/<name_with_underscores>_test.py`), with no `python/` project. It runs as `python3 .agents/skills/<name>/scripts/<name_with_underscores>.py`. The update worker makes a workspace's own single-script, dependency-free skills bare skills.

- **`validate_skill.py`** now requires:
  - for a bare skill, a script that imports only the standard library, has no PEP 723 header, does not shadow a standard-library module, and answers `--help` under `python3 -S -s`;
  - otherwise, a `python/pyproject.toml` naming `<name>-skill` and `<name_with_underscores>_skill` whenever the skill has Python;
  - a passing `uv lock --check`;
  - every entry file, and every package module with its own `if __name__ == "__main__":` block, to answer `--help` under `uv run --no-sync`;
  - no module named like a standard-library module beside a module that runs by its path, which would import it instead.

  It no longer requires PEP 723 headers.

- **New skills:** `.agents/shared/scripts/agents_shared/scaffold_skill.py <name> --description "..." [--python] [--crystallized]` writes a new skill in the spec layout (its `run.py` is a package module run by its path, with no stub in `scripts/`), runs `uv lock` and `uv sync --all-packages`, and validates it. A name or description that would not validate writes nothing.

- **Previews start faster:** `preview_app.py` loads the manifest library (and pydantic) only for `up`; `refresh` and `down` work from the preview's recorded state.

- **Docs:** `spec-summary.md` and `type-skill.md` describe the layout, the scaffold and the lazy-import rule, which has no exceptions: code whose signatures name a heavy library's types goes in a module of its own, imported inside the subcommands that need it. `running-python.md` describes the bare and venv tiers, that a script's imports decide which it is in, and that code calls workspace code by importing it, starting a process only when the call needs one of its own. update-app's `SKILL.md` says a preview syncs its worktree `--frozen` before every boot, so a dependency change there needs `uv lock` before `refresh`.

- **Going live with a merged skill:** a skill with a `python/` project runs from the workspace venv, so `lead-proxy.md`'s provisional go-live and the crystallize, heal and update go-live steps run `uv sync --all-packages --frozen` after the merge.

- **Idle and shed checks on workers:** launch-task imports `chat_background_tasks` (whether a worker is parked on a background task) and `oom_priority` (whether the OOM daemon shed it) as package dependencies of `launch-task-skill`, instead of putting their `src` dirs on `sys.path` from the launcher's checkout. It no longer passes its own checkout when it looks up the marker directory, so `chat_background_tasks` finds it from the checkout the library is installed from.

- **publish-template's GitHub and publish tools:** `github_access.py`, `github_repo.py`, `push_snapshot.py` and `record_publish.py` live in `python/publish_template_skill/` and run in the live workspace's environment, `uv run --no-sync --project /home/user/workspace "$PTM/<tool>.py"`, so they work from the worker's worktree, whose venv the assembly's clean removes. `record_publish.py` imports update-self's ledger helpers from `update_self_skill` instead of putting update-self's scripts on `sys.path`.

- **Python floor:** the root project type-checks every skill's scripts except a third party's skill, and the skill projects require Python 3.12.

- **update-self on an older Python:** the staged `update_self.py` now checks the interpreter before importing anything. On a workspace whose system Python is older than 3.12 (a local workspace from before 2026-09-14), it exits with code 75 and prints the whole procedure: stop the pass, record a `NEEDS_RECREATION` verdict with the workspace's own copy, tell the user it is a migration-required update (`migrate-workspace` moves their work), and release the update lease. Step 3a says only to stop and follow what a failing re-check prints.

- **Migration reference:** a new section on fixing ty errors in a workspace's own skills and apps. The update-self worker fixes them during the update, except an error whose only fix changes behavior the user can see, which it raises with the user instead. The command rewrites also cover the user's scheduled jobs in `data/.state/cron.d/`, which no check scans.

- **Syncing after a merge:** after merging a worker's branch that changed a `pyproject.toml` or `uv.lock` (such as a newly crystallized skill's `python/` project), the lead now runs `uv sync --all-packages --frozen`, so the new package is installed before anything runs it with `uv run --no-sync`. `running-python.md` lists this case. The update-self worker does the same before its validation suites and boots whenever the merge changed a `pyproject.toml` or `uv.lock`, including one only upstream changed, since those suites run `uv run --no-sync`.

- **Harnesses without a session-start sync:** `running-python.md` now says agents on harnesses without a session-start hook (claude and codex have one) sync themselves after a `pyproject.toml` or `uv.lock` change.

- **Ledger pointers:** publish-template, update-installed-template and update-published-template point at `update-self`'s `python/update_self_skill/update_ledger.py` for the exact `VERSION_HISTORY.md` starter block, instead of the `scripts/update_self.py` entry stub.

- **New apps at the 3.12 floor:** build-app's scaffold writes `requires-python = ">=3.12"` into a new app's `pyproject.toml`.

- **update-self's venv step:** an update that changes the backend manifests no longer copies the root venv aside and syncs it in place. It syncs the merged tree into a fresh venv beside the uv cache, through that venv's real path, pre-flights the shell and the chat from it, and switches `.venv` to it just before the restart. The previous venv is deleted once the restart is healthy, and a rollback switches the link back. The first such update on a workspace whose `.venv` is still a real directory converts it in the same step, keeping the old directory until the restart is healthy and putting it back on rollback. A later `rollback-last` re-syncs the venv for the restored tree.

- **`running-python.md`:** `.venv` is a link the workspace manages, with the one command that recreates a missing target.

update-self, build-app and the agent docs move to the app-environments layout: the built-in apps share the workspace venv, and every user-built package is a standalone project.

- **update-self runs and tests the install the services use.** The shell and chat pre-flights boot `.venv/bin/system-interface` and `.venv/bin/chat-app` (or the fresh venv the apply swaps in), the entry points supervisord runs, instead of bare names from the agent's PATH, which found per-app uv tools the services never ran. The per-app tool refresh, snapshots, rollback rebuild and shadowing sweep are gone; a change to a built-in app's `pyproject.toml` re-syncs the venv, and only `uv.lock`, the root `pyproject.toml` and the plugin manifest reinstall the mngr tool. A landed update removes the per-app tools older builds left.

- **User packages are standalone.** A user app, service or lib under `system/` (any package the root `members` does not name) has its own `uv.lock` and `.venv`, so a dependency it adds never moves the chat's versions. The update migrates old-layout ones with update-self's new `user-package-migration` command (`uv run --no-sync user-package-migration migrate --dry-run`, then `migrate --shared-lock <pre-merge lock>`; `relock` for a stale lock): it keeps their versions, turns workspace sources into editable path sources, rewrites their program lines and one-off commands, and takes them out of the root `pyproject.toml`. The worker checks each package's lock, puts the dry run in its report, and gives each converted package its suite and boot from its own venv. An apply syncs each user package it changed in place.

- **Broken user things get fixed after an update, not reported.** After a successful apply, the lead says in one chat line what it is fixing, sends a repair worker with the evidence, and finishes once it is fixed or the worker gives up (still `UPDATED`, with a detail naming what is left).

- **build-app** scaffolds a standalone project: an `app-schema` path dependency, a lock seeded from the root lock, its own test dependencies and pytest root, a linked venv, and a program line that links, syncs `--locked` and execs from its own `.venv/bin`. It no longer installs an app as a uv tool or touches the root lock.

- **Previews and isolated boots** of a user package run from its own venv (`serve_isolated_instance.py --project`). `migrate-workspace` converts the packages it lands (`convert-packages`), and `use-template` and `update-installed-template` say an older template's app needs converting. `AGENTS.md`, `running-python.md`, `service-processes.md`, `spec-summary.md` and the app and service worker guides (`type-app.md`, `type-service.md`) describe the two kinds of package, including where a user package's dependencies change and its tests run.

The notify-user skill says a reply posted into a chat room (`mngr message --start <room>`) is the notification, so the script is not run for one.

The `manage-desktop` skill describes desktops as belonging to people by convention (a desktop's `owner`, the "Left behind" desktops of people who have gone) and the shell's overview, which replaces the taskbar's desktop switcher as the place a person creates, renames, reorders, and deletes their desktops; a desktop's colour and glyph are no longer shown, so an agent names a desktop and leaves the rest to the shell (the mngr repo's `specs/multiplayer-refinements/spec.md`, section 8).

The `build-app` skill gains "Renaming an app": when an app's `display_name` changes, rename the chat titled "<old> Chat" to "<new> Chat" with `system/scripts/rename_chat.py`; the button finds the chat by its `app_chat` label whatever its title, so the title is what the rename keeps true (the mngr repo's `specs/multiplayer-refinements/spec.md`, section 9.3).

The `update-self` skill states the frontend-rebuild contract plainly: an update touching any frontend source or the shared `workspace_ui` library (which carries behavior the shell depends on from every app page, like the `shell:input` activity reports) lands only with the bundles rebuilt; its apply does this itself, and the rule guards hand-applied updates.

The manage-routines skill's timezone prose reflects that the container clock now comes from `data/.state/user_timezone`, written once by the client that created the workspace, rather than a boot-time fetch from the desktop (user-profile-state spec, phase 3B).

The vendored imbue-studio skill's cross-workspace verb table gains `minds-workspaces-account-settings` (saving a workspace's keyboard-shortcut changes to its account), synced from the pinned mngr commit for user-profile-state phase 3C.

The browser moved onto the Screen (`docs/system/specs/screen/spec.md`, sections 16 and 17):

- `agentic-browser-fleet` keeps its verbs and exit codes against the Screen service, and its skill says what changed: the browser runs on the Screen beside everything else the user runs there and no longer stops when its window closes; `new` opens the Screen's window minimized as before and `handoff` shows it; the lease is the Screen's, so a human using the Screen holds the browser too and `ls` says "human (driving the Screen)"; `screen shot` shows whatever is frontmost, so an agent raises Chromium's window with `screen activate` before relying on it; after a crash `new` restarts the same browser and the agent attaches under a fresh `playwright-cli` slug.

- A new `use-screen` skill documents the `screen` command (`run`, `windows`, `activate`, `shot`, `size`, `control acquire|release|handoff`, `open`), the lease rules with the human always winning, and xdotool on `DISPLAY=:99` and the CDP proxy as the two input paths.

- `manage-desktop` names the Screen where it named the browser (the `screen` app's `browser` launch path behind `open https://...`, the Screen's window, the Screen service's stop and start routes), and `build-app` lists the Screen's ports (8083, 8090) among the ones to avoid.

- The `use-screen` skill lists `screen browser open [URL]`, the browser launch path as a verb of the `screen` command.

- `migrate-workspace`'s legacy path map sends the old `libs/browser/` to `system/apps/screen/`, where the browser lives now, rather than to the deleted `system/apps/browser/`.

- The `use-screen` and `agentic-browser-fleet` skills describe `handoff` as the lease does it: the Screen goes to the human pinned (no other agent can take it until they give it back), with the agent first in line to resume; the human's first input claims it, and their "Give control back" or leaving hands it to the agent.

The update apply (`update-self`) carries a workspace that ran the browser app onto the Screen:

- The old `browser` uv tool goes the way every per-app tool install does under the fresh-venv apply: once the merged tree is live and healthy, the apply runs the sweep the build's `tool_env.py drop-app-tools` runs (`tool_env.remove_app_tool_installs`), which removes the tool environments older builds installed editable from an app directory, console scripts included, and only warns when it cannot. The Screen runs from the workspace venv, so nothing is installed over the `agentic-browser-fleet` script the old tool owned.

- The Screen's viewer is one of the frontend bundles the apply builds, installs from the worker (`--worker-bundle screen=<path>`), snapshots and verifies, beside the shell's, the chat's, Getting Started's, Files' and Routines'; a change under `system/apps/screen/frontend/` rebuilds like any other frontend's.

- Before the restart it removes every registry row (`data/.state/apps.toml`) whose supervisord program the merged tree no longer declares, through `forward_port.py --remove`, so the old browser app's row stops offering a dead "Browser" tile in the launcher and a dead origin to the share gateway. A row with no program is never touched, and a program the tree still runs registers itself again on its next start.

- `migrate-workspace`'s legacy-layout reference sends `libs/browser/` to `system/apps/screen/`, as its path map already did.

- The apply no longer races the boot-time env-converge for the dpkg lock: its post-success `env-converge upgrade` step first waits (bounded, 15 minutes) for the one-shot env-converge program to finish -- the apply's own services restart re-runs it, and a unit with new pins (the Screen's stack) can keep it installing for minutes. Found by the upgrade end-to-end test, where the apply's `apt_full_upgrade` step failed with "Could not get lock /var/lib/dpkg/lock-frontend" while the Screen stack installed.

### system

- Moved the Lima guest image (`[providers.lima]` `default_image_url_*`) to the Debian 13 genericcloud `20261026-2643` release, the one carrying the CVE-2026-98432 kernel fix (`linux` 6.12.113-1), matching the `mngr_lima` library default and the gen-2 slice guest image, so new desktop Lima VMs boot the fixed kernel.

The mngr pin moves from the multiplayer branch's export to the public mirror of mngr main (`97b6345850`, the merge of the multiplayer refinements), so workspaces run the released mngr with the same changes.

- The bug-report collector no longer asks mngr for a stopped agent's pane (it has none), and reads panes and chat transcripts four at a time instead of one after another. On a 35-agent workspace that was 71 serial mngr calls and about two minutes; on a loaded one it overran the 300 s collection budget and the report lost its whole archive.

- mngr is pinned to a build that lets the chat app name the providers it compacts agents on.

`docs/specs/chat-send-failure-system.md` covers mngr's `submission_unconfirmed`, `agent_not_found`, `not_submitted` and `state_unknown` send-failure kinds, and what the chat app does on its own before a failure reaches the user. It sends a message once more after `submission_unconfirmed` and `unknown` to the same place, answering a send that then lands `"resent"`, which the page shows as a "Sent again" line under the message that a second copy folds into; after `agent_not_found` by discovery; after `not_submitted` to the same place. It tries again after 1, 2 and 4 seconds after `not_ready` and `state_unknown`, and once more at once after `agent_unreachable`. The spec says what the failure notice offers when that repeat fails too, why a still-unconfirmed send gets Send again and no Force, how the chat takes its composer copy back out once the agent's turn for it arrives, and which harnesses can return an unconfirmed send at all.

mngr is pinned to the commit that adds `not_submitted` and reads Claude's screen for a send it has waited out.

- In newly created workspaces the `bootstrap` window, and in every workspace github-sync's program line and the user-service example in `service-processes.md` now start their entry point from `.venv/bin` after a `uv sync --all-packages --frozen`, as host-backup, share-gateway and env-converge already did, so no `uv` process stays resident as a parent of supervisord or any program. A failed boot-time sync still starts `bootstrap` on the existing venv, so a workspace with a broken dependency tree stays reachable. A workspace created before this release keeps the `uv run bootstrap` window it was created with: mngr records an agent's windows when it creates it.

- The claude and codex `SessionStart` hooks run `system/scripts/session_start_sync.sh`, which syncs the venv `--frozen` from the committed `uv.lock` and never rewrites it: a lock that has drifted from `pyproject.toml` is reported once, for whoever is changing dependencies to relock. Worker provisioning syncs `--frozen` too.

- One-off commands in `AGENTS.md`, config and scripts use `uv run --no-sync`, so following an instruction never relocks or syncs the workspace. The new root test `system/test_python_launch_rules.py` fails on any supervisord program (user-added drop-ins included) or `.mngr/settings.toml` window that runs under `uv run`, and on any plain `uv run` in a tracked doc, prompt, config or script, in a string or argv of the workspace's Python, or in a living `contracts.md`; an existing workspace's own services and docs get rewritten during the update merge.

- The secrets guard recognises `uv run --no-sync` / `--frozen` / `--quiet` in front of `with_secrets.py` and `request_secret.py`; any other `uv run` option in front of them is still blocked.

This release turns the workspace's scripts into packages. An existing workspace's own skills, services and docs are migrated during the update by following `.agents/skills/update-self/references/python-packaging-migration.md`.

- `system/scripts` is one uv project with two packages. `workspace_bare_scripts` runs under the system `python3` with no venv and imports only the standard library (and the stdlib-only libraries its hook stubs put on `sys.path`). `workspace_scripts` (the changelog gate, the docs viewer, the view refresh and `verify_app`) runs from the root venv.

- A script runs from its module by path. A thin entry file stays at the old path only where something outside this release runs it (Imbue Studio, minds_evals, the web client, mngr's pin scripts, update-self on an older release's tree, the app programs users' scaffolded apps run) or where it has to put a directory on `sys.path`; each says why in its docstring. A bare one also says it finds its package only because its own directory is first on `sys.path`, so it must be run as `python3 <path>`, never with `-I`, `-P` or `PYTHONSAFEPATH`. `run_in_background.py`, `tool_env.py` and `list_mngr_plugins.py` run from `system/scripts/workspace_bare_scripts/`, and the changelog gate, the docs viewer and `verify_app` from `system/scripts/workspace_scripts/`. `verify_app` no longer re-runs itself under `.venv/bin/python` when playwright is missing; it says to run it with `uv run --no-sync`.

- The four guard hooks (pipe into tail/head, latchkey request, secrets, tk standalone) run their checks through one entry, `system/scripts/agent_hook_check.py <check>`, instead of a wrapper each. Only it, the rewrite hook's entry, the two background-task entries and the skill entry files that run with no venv (update-self's, and publish-template's two manifest tools) still edit `sys.path`.

- `background_tasks.py`, `claude_background_task_hooks.py` and `vendor_mngr_skill.py` move into `workspace_bare_scripts`, with their tests beside them. Each keeps its path as an entry file, since all three run by that path under the system `python3`: Imbue Studio and its admin and eval tools run `background_tasks.py`, Claude's Stop and SessionStart hooks run `claude_background_task_hooks.py`, and CI and mngr's pin bump run `vendor_mngr_skill.py`. `system/test_external_entry_paths.py` now runs all three. The two background-task entry files put `system/libs/chat_background_tasks` on `sys.path` (the hooks' entry also puts `oom_priority` there, for the rewrite hook's command parsing), so they are counted among the import-path edits. The modules import the library normally.

- `forward_port` has a `register()` / `remove()` API, which its command line now runs, and `message_chat` a `send()`. The shared preview script registers its servers, and launch-task and the browser fleet send their messages, through them in-process instead of starting `python3` on the scripts; `send()` takes the repo root to read the registry from and run `mngr` in. `verify_app --open` / `--refresh` surfaces the page through `workspace_layout` in-process instead of running `uv run --no-sync workspace-layout`.

- The root workspace adds the `system/scripts`, `.agents/shared/scripts` and `.agents/skills/*/python` members, so skill dependencies resolve in the one `uv.lock`.

- The CI changelog job runs the gate (`system/scripts/workspace_scripts/check_changelog_entries.py`) from a `uv sync --frozen --package workspace-scripts` venv.

- New root checks:
  - `system/test_entry_point_import_cost.py` fails an entry point -- an entry file, or a package module with its own `if __name__ == "__main__":` block -- that loads pydantic, loguru, click, tenacity, httpx or asyncio at import, with no exceptions. A heavy module that another one it loads imports counts toward that one, so it names pydantic rather than the asyncio pydantic loads on Python 3.12.
  - `system/test_external_entry_paths.py` runs every path that Imbue Studio, CI and older update-self releases call by path. The bare paths run with no site-packages; the one venv-tier path, launch-task's `create_worker.py`, runs from the root venv.
  - `system/test_python_launch_rules.py` fails a `python3 <path>.py` that names a venv-tier or missing script, and a `uv run <path>.py` whose script is not in the tree, so a path that moved is rewritten wherever it is written down. It also counts, tests included, the code that edits the import path (`sys.path` under any alias, `monkeypatch.syspath_prepend`, `site.addsitedir`, a non-empty `PYTHONPATH` handed to a subprocess, a pytest `pythonpath` setting) and the code that loads a module from a file (`spec_from_file_location`, `spec_from_loader`, the file loaders, `runpy.run_path`, `exec(compile(...))`), and fails when either count rises. A skill listed in `.agents/third-party-skills.toml` is not counted, and the import-cost and launch checks do not read its files; `system/test_meta_ratchets.py` fails on an entry naming a skill that is not in the tree. A `sys.path` edit may only add a directory the bare type check searches (where the bare packages and the stdlib-only libraries live), written as path arithmetic on `Path(__file__)`; publish-template's two `uv run --no-project` tools and update-self's runtime `oom_priority` import are named exceptions.
  - `system/test_python_launch_rules.py` also counts the places non-test code names one of the workspace's own programs to run as a process -- a path to a runnable module, `-m` with one of its packages, or one of its packages' commands in an argv -- and fails when the count rises. `running-python.md` lists when a process is still the right call.
  - The plain-`uv run` check no longer reads files that link into `system/vendor/`. Once the mngr assets were fetched, `docs/system/style_guide.md` resolved to mngr's style guide and failed the check inside a workspace.
  - The plain-`uv run` check now covers script runs too: a `uv run <path>.py` with no `--no-sync` fails it, and so does a Python argv that starts `uv run` with a computed program and no `--no-sync` before it.
  - `system/test_meta_ratchets.py` requires a `pyproject.toml` in every skill `python/` dir. Without one, every `uv` command in the workspace fails.

- The Datalib app's launcher, `system/apps/datalib/launch_datalib_http.py`, counts as a bare entry point, like oom_priority's own scripts: its supervisord program runs it under the system `python3`, so the `sys.path` insert it uses to import `oom_priority` is one of the counted import-path edits. Its tests import it by name instead of loading it from its file.

- The bug-report collector runs as a `Collector` object that takes its container paths and class budgets as arguments. Its tests build one per test instead of loading a fresh copy of the module by path. What the collector collects is unchanged.

- The supervisord program readers in `system/test_app_manifests.py` and `system/test_supervisord_layout.py` share one helper, `oom_priority.supervisord_testing.supervisord_commands`, instead of loading each other's test files by path. The root checks that skip vendored content share `system/vendor_testing.py`.
