The chat app's pytest config also deletes a passing test's `tmp_path` as soon as it finishes and keeps only the latest session's leftovers (`tmp_path_retention_policy = "failed"`, `tmp_path_retention_count = 1`), the same as the root config, so its test runs stop filling the workspace's tmpfs `/tmp`.

The note update-self sends a chat it paused for an update renders as a one-line notice labelled "Workspace updated" (or "Workspace update not applied"), on every harness.

`open=providers` in the chat root's URL opens the provider chooser once on arrival, for the Imbue Studio app's sign-in button.

### system/apps/datalib

The Datalib app now serves `data/.skills/datalib/Default`: the skill's folder is a libraries folder laid out like the desktop app's `~/Datalib`, with one folder per library, and the app serves the `Default` one. The launcher moves a store that an earlier workspace wrote at `data/.skills/datalib` itself into `Default` before it reads the token, with two atomic renames through a staging sibling (`data/.skills/datalib.moving-to-Default`), and finishes the move on the next start if it was interrupted between them. It follows the desktop app's rules for moving a library: only a store at the real libraries folder is moved (the library is known by where it is on disk, whatever spelling of its path the launcher is given), a store a datalib process still holds is left for the next start, and a top-level `data_root` in the moved `config.toml` that names the old folder is dropped. A folder that holds a store of its own and a non-empty `Default` makes the launcher refuse to start, naming both. The token's path is now `data/.skills/datalib/Default/system/api-token`.

Datalib can be shown in Studio's windows: its launcher sets `DATALIB_FRAME_ANCESTORS` to the places Studio frames it from, the desktop app's local origins and, for a shared workspace, Imbue's content domains and hosted chrome origins. It takes effect with a datalib that reads the variable (imbue-ai/datalib#1318); an older one ignores it.

### system/apps/files

Downloading a file or folder from Files works inside Imbue Studio. Before, it offered to save `download.txt` (or the file's name with `.txt` in place of its extension), and the download failed.

- Download loads the file through the shared `startDownload` helper rather than a `download` link, whose request went without the workspace's session.

- The server serves a file's `?download` as an attachment under its own name, alongside a folder's `?zip`. A file shared live from a computer gets the same treatment, but only when the computer actually sent the file.

- A download the server refuses shows a toast saying why, such as "Couldn't download notes.txt: There's nothing at /notes.txt." A missing path asked for as `?download` or `?zip` is answered in plain words, not with the not-found page.

### system/apps/getting_started

Getting Started no longer opens its own window on a workspace's first visit: a new workspace opens on the welcome chat alone, and the desktop's show-around tour introduces the apps. The first-visit opener and its ledger are gone from the app; a ledger an older workspace wrote is left alone.

This app's pytest config deletes a passing test's `tmp_path` as soon as it finishes and keeps only the latest session's leftovers (`tmp_path_retention_policy = "failed"`, `tmp_path_retention_count = 1`), the same as the root config. Leftover test directories in the workspace's tmpfs `/tmp` held sandbox memory until deleted.

### system/apps/routines

New: the Routines app, one window over everything that runs on a schedule. The list shows each routine's health, schedule and next run, and its last run; a routine's page has Run now, On/Off, Change schedule, Fix it (a chat briefed on the failure) and Remove, and its run history with each run's summary and a link to its chat; a run's page shows its log as is. A field at the top of the list describes a routine to add, which opens a chat for the agent to write it; the rows group under the display names of the apps they belong to. A routine's notification from the Imbue Studio feed lands on its page.

The schedule dialog edits the cadence, the time of day, the weekdays and the day of the month. The pages re-read every 30 seconds, and every 5 seconds while a run is going, with the polling held while the schedule editor or the Remove confirmation is open; a re-read that fails keeps the page's data and says so in a toast. The routine's own chat opens through a plain link, the rows group by the app itself (an app called Workspace stays apart from the workspace's own rows), and the pages' content-named bundle files are cached for a year.

Every list row shows its last run and that run's summary, beside the health's detail when there is one. The run page keeps the end of a growing log in view while a run is going, unless the reader scrolled up. Fix it is the page's primary control.

A run's whole log has a page of its own under the same navigation header (`/<id>/runs/<run id>/log`) instead of the bare text route, and every run row on a routine's page is one link to the run, drawn like a routine's row on the list.

The `launcher_rank` comment in `app.toml` names the app after it, System Monitor, by its current name (it was Memory & disk when the Routines app was written).

### system/apps/system_interface

The pytest configuration requires the pytest-workspace-env plugin (`required_plugins`), so a test run that cannot load it, and would let a test see the environment of the agent running it, stops before collecting anything.

The avatar chooser's "Original SVG" link downloads inside Imbue Studio. It went through a `download` link, whose request went without the workspace's session; it now uses the shared `startDownload` helper and shows a toast if the download fails.

- The update notice's list of apps can now include an ordinary app: a careful pass that also changed one keeps it in the rollback record, so the banner names it and a rollback restarts it.

- The tests' WebSocket client now also delivers messages that arrive in the same socket read as the handshake response. Before, a test of the `/api/ws` replay could time out when the server's first messages arrived together with the accept.

The shell's page now relays a message the Imbue Studio chrome posts into it whose type the embed contract does not define (a notification's `destination`, such as `minds:show-routine`) to the app whose manifest registers the type, through `relay.ts` (`setEmbedderAppMessageHandler`), since the contract's endpoint drops such a type before `embed.ts`'s observer sees it. Opening a routine's notification in the desktop app now shows the routine's page.

The desktop launcher's Enter now sends a typed text to the main chat: the chat app lists "Send to main chat" first among its text rows, ahead of "New Chat" (now Cmd+Enter, or Ctrl+Enter off a Mac). The inventory test expects the new row.


"Design your own..." in the avatar chooser now drafts its prompt into the main chat instead of whichever chat the pinned window shows: a launch into a window can leave out the window's page (`sends_window_path: false` on the target), so the app puts the text where a text with no chat of its own goes.

- An app can now take custom-scheme links (`slack:`, `paseo:`, `vscode:`) by registering a message handler for `open:<scheme>` (`open:slack`). The shell announces `opensCustomSchemeLinks` to Imbue Studio, which then hands it such links from the workspace's pages, and a page's click on one comes to the shell too. A custom-scheme link no app takes goes back to Imbue Studio, which asks before opening it in the app of the user's system. With an older Imbue Studio, which shows a popup of one as an empty window, the shell launches the link by navigating its own page to it; in a plain browser (a share link, `minds run`) it opens in a new tab, as a web link does.

The desktop gets a show-around tour. It begins the first time the workspace's agent goes to work, so the user learns the product while waiting for a reply: a card pops out beside the agent's avatar and walks through the agent, the workspace, the chat window (whose Next snaps the chat to the right half of the desktop, revealing the shortcuts), the apps, connecting data, backups, sharing, devices, feedback, AI providers, and durable apps, ending at the launcher. The agent answering interrupts the tour: the card stays, the next Next shows "The agent is waiting for you. We'll resume the tour later", and the tour resumes from the card that would have come next the next time the agent works. The page's `tour_start_ms` query parameter makes the tour wait for a task that has been running that long instead of starting on the first message. A card about a control of the Imbue Studio chrome (the workspace switcher, a workspace tab, the help button) asks the chrome to ring it through the new `minds:highlight-chrome` embed-contract message; the words never depend on the ring. Exiting early leaves one badge pointing at the launcher, whose new "Show me around" row runs the tour again from the first card at any time. The phone layout, where the tour does not run, never lists the row.

What the tour has done is one record the shell keeps in `data/.state/system_interface/tour.json` (`is_seen` and `resume_index`), read and written through `GET` and `POST /api/tour`. The tour's three pictures (the connectors strip, a loop of service logos sliding by; a computer and a phone; the provider menu) are hosted on the onboarding-media bucket under content-addressed names, not bundled, and the shell's page policy admits images from that origin.

The pinned chat window now first shows at most of the backdrop (a margin in on every side) rather than the right half, so a new workspace opens on the welcome chat; the tour's chat card is what snaps it aside.

For now the tour runs once per workspace; limiting it to a user's first workspace waits for the cross-workspace data sync.

The tour's words follow the v2 copy document, adapted to the shipped tour (it pauses when the agent answers rather than bringing the user back, and its connect card carries both the services and the folders): the intro, agent, connect, security, devices, feedback, and last cards, and the pause notice, are reworded, and a card's text may hold several short paragraphs (a blank line in the text; the card draws each with a gap).

This app's pytest config deletes a passing test's `tmp_path` as soon as it finishes and keeps only the latest session's leftovers (`tmp_path_retention_policy = "failed"`, `tmp_path_retention_count = 1`), the same as the root config. Leftover test directories in the workspace's tmpfs `/tmp` held sandbox memory until deleted.

### system/apps/system_monitor

Memory & disk becomes System Monitor: the app adds CPU and gains a view per resource. The overview shows three tiles (CPU as a share of the cores, memory and disk as a share of their totals, with the last 10 minutes under the first two), the breakdown of what is using the workspace with CPU and memory columns, and the recent events (programs the memory guard stopped, and busy stretches of CPU above 90% with the chats and programs that caused them). The CPU view (`/cpu`) has the number of processes running, a chart over 10 minutes, an hour or a day, the breakdown sorted by share, and the busy stretches; the Memory view (`/memory`) is the previous page's content with the guard's 90% mark drawn in; the Disk view (`/disk`) shows the disk, the state of the backups (from the backup service's events, with a link to its README), and measures what is on the disk only when asked, saying which rows it could not measure (or that the walk failed, with a way to try again).

The graphs now come from the `resource_sampler` program (`system/services/oom_priority`), so they stay whole across the app stopping between windows; the app no longer samples memory itself. New routes: `/api/history?span=1h|24h`, `/api/disk`, and `POST /api/disk/scan`; `/api/stats` carries `cpu`, `events`, both graphs' `history`, and a `cpu` share on every breakdown row.

The breakdown now adds up: a group's memory is its programs' anonymous memory (what stopping them frees), the Shared row is the shared memory segments they map, the System row holds the rest in both accounting modes, and its CPU is what the other rows fall short of the tile. The Workspace row lists the workspace's own programs (the chat app, the desktop, each service by a plain name, the boot-time environment setup as "Environment setup", and what no program started by its command), and rows with nothing under them are hidden. Every chat, code checker and user app has a Stop button (an "x" on hover, always on touch screens) that asks before it stops the chat through the chat app, the checkers by signal, or the app through supervisord (`POST /api/stop`; an app that quit on its own since the page last refreshed counts as quit); the workspace's own programs have none. The disk view says the figure is the machine's whole disk, puts what is using it above the backups, and its walk lists the workspace's folders (with hints for `.venv`, `.git` and the like), each package cache, and the system software behind "Everything else".

Inside the app, the agent records are read by one `programs.chats` reader (the separate `chat_names` and `chat_ids` readers are gone), a Stop request's kind is dispatched with `match`, and the API document's `usage_mode` description names the accounting as it now is (anonymous memory, a System row in both modes).

The Workspace row names the agent observer "Agent manager" and the owner-exec daemon "Web access", and splits what no program started into "SSH access" (sshd and its sessions), "Internal system" (tini, the bootstrap and its uv wrapper, supervisord, the services agent's tmux and shell) and "Other".

Programs stopped to free memory keep their plain description and exact command now that earlyoom's log puts a UTC time before every line (oom_priority's `earlyoom-stamp`). The app's reader of that log expected each line to start with earlyoom's own text, so it matched no stop in a stamped log; it now drops the time first, and still reads the unstamped lines written before the change.

### system/libs/app_manifest

New `app-manifest pass-scope --creation <type>:<name> [...] [--diff-base REF] [--lead-ref REF] [--out FILE]` writes the scope file for a harden pass over several creations (`app:`, `skill:`, `service:`, `shared:`): each creation's footprint, and one diff split into the files some creation accounts for and those none does. A standalone service (or an app with no `app.toml` yet) is scoped by its directory plus its package-named and `<name>-<role>` programs. A creation named twice, directly or by an app's name and package directory, is refused.

With `--lead-ref`, the diff separates the pass's own work from other chats': it gains `fork_point` (unaffected by milestones the lead merged), `others` (changed files in no footprint and not the pass's own), and `lockfile_base` (where a changed `uv.lock` is compared from, so the hardened change's own upgrade is tested). `outside_footprint` lists only the pass's own changes.

`select-tests --scope-file FILE` selects every changed file except `others`, and refuses a scope file with no fork point or whose diff does not reach `HEAD`, and a dirty working tree.

`pass-scope --lead-ref` records what a branch merged in from the lead after leaving its line (a catch-up): `incoming_base` and `incoming`, the changed files of those lead commits, both empty for a branch that merged in nothing.

`select-tests --scope-file` runs, for each incoming file, only the suites and npm packages of the pass's own creations that it reaches through a declared dependency (a package, a `uv.lock` upgrade, a shared frontend package, or the root project's `pyproject.toml` / `conftest.py`), not the changed package's own suite, its other dependents, or the full root suite. A shared script in the pass gets the full root suite. When an incoming `uv.lock` cannot be compared, every creation's own suite runs, with a note `select-tests` now prints even when it selects nothing. A gate whose branch merged nothing from the lead selects exactly what it did before.

### system/libs/bootstrap

- The README bounces an app after a code change with `verify_app.py <name> --restart`, which skips the 30 s `startsecs` wait, and keeps `supervisorctl restart <name>` for a daemon with no port.

The bootstrap writes the routines tick cron entry (`/etc/cron.d/routines`, `routines tick` once a minute through the routines env wrapper) at every boot beside the recovery guard, and first runs `routines migrate-cron` so a workspace's cron entries from before routines existed become definitions; the `data/.state/cron.d` install still runs for whatever the migration leaves there.

### system/libs/chat_background_tasks

`markers.is_process_live(pid, pid_start)` is the liveness rule on its own (alive, and the same process where `/proc` reports a start time), which `is_task_live` and the routines runner both use.

### system/libs/pytest_workspace_env

The plugin now clears the environment an mngr agent runs with before any conftest is imported: every variable starting with `MNGR_`, `MINDS_`, `CODE_GUARDIAN_`, `REVIEWER_` or `CLAUDE_`, plus `CLAUDECODE`, `MAIN_CLAUDE_SESSION_ID`, `TMUX`, `TMUX_PANE`, `LLM_USER_PATH`, `ORIGINAL_CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`. CI has none of these, so a test that read one without setting it passed in CI and failed whenever an agent ran it, as update-self's test gate does. Seen with `create_worker_test.py`, which failed one test inside any agent on 0.8.6. Tests, conftests and the subprocesses tests start no longer see them; a test that needs one sets it itself. The session header lists what was cleared. The root, chat and system interface pytest configurations name the plugin in `required_plugins`, so a run that cannot load it stops before collecting anything.

### system/libs/routines

New: the routines library, everything in the workspace that runs on a schedule. One TOML definition per routine under `system/routines/`, a scheduler (interval or one-off, time of day, weekdays, day of the month, catch-up after downtime, retry after a failed run), one runner for command runs and skill runs (which wake the routine's own chat and wait for the agent's turn through the chat app), per-routine state, an append-only run ledger with a log per run, notifications to the Imbue Studio feed (headed by the routine's title) after repeated failures, on recovery and when an agent waits on the user, whether the agent was woken by a skill routine or by `routines wake` from a command routine's run, the `routines` command for agents, the cron env wrapper, and `routines migrate-cron`, which converts the cron entries a workspace wrote before. The listing names the apps routines belong to (`app_names`, from the app registry), a run in flight is told from a reused pid by the process's start time, and a spawned run's own output goes to its run log.

`routines wake` names the chat after the routine and waits as long as the routine's `timeout` says when the routine is defined (`--title` and `--timeout` still override), so a command routine that wakes its agent is recorded as a skill run is.

`routines migrate-cron` also converts a plain cron line's weekday lists and ranges (`1-5`, `1,3,5`) and a runner job id with capitals or underscores, leaves an entry whose routine already exists in place, and points every entry it leaves with cron at the env wrapper's new path. The command refuses a `--days` or `--once` it cannot read, a mistyped `--run-id`, and a `routines log` for a run the routine never had, each in one line; an empty `--at`, `--days` or `--app` clears the field on `edit`; a wake inside a run never waits past the run's own time. The Fix brief quotes the last finished run's output. A skill run reads a turn longer than one transcript page to its end, so its summary is the agent's last message and a long turn is never mistaken for one that is still going. A skill run whose agent worked and went idle without answering ends failed a minute later, instead of waiting out the routine's timeout and interrupting an idle chat. A state file that cannot be opened is an error rather than a fresh start, and one whose content does not parse is kept beside the fresh one (`state.json.bad`) when the next write replaces it. `routines add` and `edit` refuse `--every` beside `--once`, and `--skill` beside a command, instead of keeping whichever came last. `routines migrate-cron` converts an entry file whole or not at all, leaves a reversed weekday range with cron, and skips a line whose duration or time of day it cannot read instead of stopping the whole pass. A routine may not be called `events`, the run ledger's directory beside the routines' own state. A skill run the chat app refuses to interrupt at its deadline is still recorded as timed out, and a run spawned by the Routines app is collected once it exits.

A manual start (`routines run <id>`, the app's Run now) answers its receipt once the run has taken hold, so a page read right after it shows the run; a run record a dead runner left behind no longer counts as a run in flight for a start or a removal. A skill run waits out a chat app that is unreachable mid-turn for two minutes (a restart, a bounce) instead of failing at the first poll. `routines wake` inside a command run leaves how it ended (a timed-out wake is a timed-out run) and its warnings in the run's `result.json`, which the runner records. A definition commit is retried only when another writer holds the index or a merge is in progress.

A run the tick closes off as interrupted counts as a failed attempt (the streak grows and the feed is told at the threshold), and the tick first stops the command a dead runner left running, whose process group the state records. A run records itself in the state before the ledger, so a runner that dies between the two is reaped. The ledger's appends and rotation share a lock. A run tries its lock a few times before it counts as refused, nothing probes the lock to ask whether a run is going, and a manual start that loses the routine to a run arriving at that moment is refused rather than handed a receipt. A message the chat app holds for a handoff is waited out: a held clear settles before the transcript cursor is read, and a held skill command gets two minutes to start.

The cron migration leaves the Imbue Studio app's `update-self-dispatch` cron entry in place: the app owns and rewrites that entry, so it is never converted into a routine.

### system/libs/tk_command_parsing

- The parser reads an unquoted backslash-newline as the shell does, a line continuation that joins the two lines, instead of a word at the head of the next command; `tk close <id> "<summary>" && \` followed by `tk start <next>` on the next line is one step boundary to the standalone-tk hook, and a `tail` after `| \` is seen by the pipe guard.

### system/libs/workspace_layout

The tests' own fixture that cleared `MINDS_CHAT_ID` and `MNGR_AGENT_ID` is gone: the pytest-workspace-env plugin now clears the whole agent environment for every test run.

### system/libs/workspace_ui

New `startDownload` helper, which the workspace's built-in pages (Files, the chat, the shell) now use to download a file of their own. An app built in a workspace that offers downloads through `download` links is not changed, and still fails inside Imbue Studio until it uses the helper too.

- It loads the file in a hidden frame instead of clicking a link with a `download` attribute. Inside Imbue Studio, the browser sends a `download` link's request without the workspace's session cookie, so the workspace refused it. The browser then offered to save the refusal, named `download.txt` (or the file's own name with `.txt` in place of its extension).

- If the server answers with something other than the file, the helper hands the page a note, "Couldn't download <name>", with the server's own words when it sent plain text.

`requestJson(method, url, body?)` in `models/http.ts` is the JSON API call with any method (a body only when given, never from the browser's cache), which `postJson` now calls; the Routines app reads and changes its routines through it.

`embed.ts` exports `isContractEmbedderMessageType(type)`, whether a chrome message's type is one the embed contract defines (and so one its endpoint dispatches to the observer); the shell's relay hands on the chrome's other messages (a notification's `destination`) itself.

- `classifyLink` now calls a custom-scheme link (`slack:`, `vscode:`: any scheme a browser does not load itself) external, and `externalLinkMessageType` names its message `open:<scheme>` (`open:slack`). A file and line or a host and port written without a scheme (`q4.md:12`, `localhost:3000/app`), which parses as a custom-scheme URL, is unroutable, as is any custom-scheme link of that shape (`sms:5551234`; `sms:+15551234` stays a link). The app contract's new `isCustomSchemeUrl` is held to the Imbue Studio desktop app's rule by the shared link vectors.

- A framed page's click on a custom-scheme link now goes to the shell (`shell:open-link`) like a `mailto:` link, instead of being left to the browser.

- `announceReadyToEmbedder` takes `opensCustomSchemeLinks` and sends it with `minds:workspace-ready`.

`embed.ts` exports `HIGHLIGHT_CHROME` (`minds:highlight-chrome`, embed contract v9): the workspace asks the Imbue Studio chrome to ring one of its own controls (`workspace-switcher`, `permissions`, `settings`, `share`, `help`) while the desktop's show-around tour talks about it, or to clear the ring with `null`. Probed off the vendored contract snapshot with a literal fallback, as the other newer constants are, so it works before the mngr pin moves.

### system/services/caretaker

The Caretaker is a routine (`system/routines/caretaker.toml`, off by default, turned on from the Routines app or with `routines enable caretaker`) rather than a cron entry two skills wrote and removed. Its check wakes the agent through `routines wake caretaker`, so the run records the chat, and it adds a fifth finding, routines that are failing, overdue, broken or waiting on the user; `--only routines` runs that finding alone, the shape a lighter daily check can take.

A routines listing the check cannot read is logged in the run, rather than passing as nothing to report.

### system/services/env_converge

`template_manifest.validate_template_tree` checks that the thumbnail is inert -- no `<script>`, no `<foreignObject>`, no `on*=` event attributes -- on every run, including the skeleton check right after assembly. The publish flow used to check this with a separate grep before the push.

`template_manifest.secret_references_in` is the one scan for the secret files a template runs under, shared by the validator and the publish flow's manifest writer. It covers only the supervisord programs and `mcp-servers.json` under the recipe's include paths, and reads program configs with supervisord's own comment rules, so the base's `host-backup` and `share-gateway` programs no longer fail every template's validation. An included program config that does not parse is reported as a problem. `is_covered_by` is the include-path test the env.d unit check also uses.

### system/services/oom_priority

A memory band for the Routines app (`routines`, between Files and Getting Started): a small page over the routines library's state that stores nothing of its own, so a shed costs one reload.

Added the `resource_sampler` program (`bin/resource_sampler.py`, policy in `resource_sampler.py`): every 5 s it reads each process's `/proc/<pid>/stat` once and records overall CPU (from the change in the sum of own plus reaped-children time, the only accounting that exists under gVisor) and memory under `data/.state/system-monitor/` (the last 10 minutes, a day of minute averages, and `cpu_stretch` events crediting a stretch of CPU above 90% to the registered agents and supervised programs that caused it) for the System Monitor app. It has its own service band, one past the app's, so it is the first built-in service shed.

The memory reader the app used (`meminfo.read_meminfo`) and the supervisord control-socket reader (`supervisor_rpc.supervised_pids`) moved into this package so the sampler and the app share them.

`supervisor_rpc` gained `stop_program`, which asks supervisord over its socket to stop one program (the System Monitor app's Quit for a user app); a program that is not running counts as stopped. The README's resource sampler section names the module and both of its functions.

`oom_priority.testing` gained `fake_supervisord`, a stand-in for supervisord's control socket that this package's tests and the System Monitor app's share.

The `publish_cgroup_meminfo` program (local docker workspaces under runc) now publishes MemAvailable as the cgroup limit minus usage plus only the inactive file cache, the same signal the kubelet evicts on and the same change as the gen-2 VM's publisher in mngr. It used to add the active file cache and reclaimable slab too. Near the limit those are what the kernel thrashes rather than frees, so the figure could not fall far enough for earlyoom's SIGKILL threshold to fire before the cgroup OOM killer did.

earlyoom's log now says when each line was written. earlyoom runs through `run_with_timestamped_output.sh`, which execs it (supervisord still signals earlyoom itself) with both of its output streams going through `earlyoom-stamp` into `/var/log/supervisor/earlyoom-stderr.log`, each line prefixed with its UTC time to the millisecond. `earlyoom-stamp` is in earlyoom's `--avoid` list, since earlyoom's own output goes through it. Without timestamps, a workspace's OOM kill could not be lined up against what earlyoom was doing at the time.

## [minds-v0.8.7] - 2026-10-19

### .agents

The file-sharing skill now says the permission dialog appears in Imbue Studio on the user's computer (was "on their machine"), so the agent keeps "machine" for the compute a workspace runs on.

`update-self`'s copy of `run_in_background.py` matches the one in `system/scripts/` again: it marks the chat as waiting on the run while the command runs, and has the new `--keep-host-awake` flag.

A worker parked on a background command of its own is no longer declared stalled. `create_worker.py`'s idle check, the one behind `await`'s exit 76, now counts a worker idle only when it has ended its turn and its chat is not busy: a command it started through `run_in_background.py`, or one of Claude's own background tasks, keeps it busy until the report reaches it. The check reads the markers through the `chat_background_tasks` library and treats a tree without that library as having no busy chats. Exit 76's message says the worker "is no longer busy". `lead-proxy.md` drops the advice to wait on one's own background commands with `sleep 60` (needed only to stay clear of that check), says why ending the turn is safe, and lists both things that keep a worker from reading idle. `freeing-memory.md` says a chat waiting on a background task is never offered for stopping, and `update-self`'s hand-off step and its run-status notes say the lead's chat reads busy, not "waiting for you", while it waits on its worker.

The File Viewer is called Files in the skills that mention it, and the update process builds, snapshots, and verifies the Files bundle (`system/apps/files/static/`) alongside the other three frontends, including a worker's `--worker-bundle files=<path>`.

The build-app scaffold's starter `runner.py` now serves every HTML page under a `Content-Security-Policy` (scripts only from the app's own origin plus the starter's inline shell-contract script by hash, same-origin fetches, sockets and images, inline styles, frames of any http(s) page, no plugins), with `inline_script_source` for admitting another inline script, a `report-uri` pointing at a new `/_csp-report` route that logs every resource the browser blocked to stderr (so a CDN script, font or API a page pulls in without its origin in the policy shows up in the supervisor log, where `check-app-errors` finds it, instead of failing silently; a blocked inline script is logged with its line and first characters, which the policy's `'report-sample'` asks the browser for, and the hash remedy; a block caused by a browser extension is not logged), and the skill says to keep the policy, that anything from another origin is blocked until the matching directive admits it, and where the log line is.

The datalib skill's `sync_request` tests: the fake Datalib server reads a POST's body before refusing it, so the refused-token test sees the 401 instead of a reset connection.

The visiting-agent primer's apps table says what each app is for and where it describes its API (the manifest's `description` and `api_schema_path`), and tells an agent to fetch that OpenAPI document before reading an app's code. The `build-app` skill's scaffolder registers the schema route, writes both manifest keys and generates the test that keeps the document honest in every new app; the scaffolded views carry docstrings, and the skill explains what an app owes the document (a docstring per view, which the generated test requires; models for validated routes) and that `--description` is the manifest's one-line description of at most 200 characters, which the scaffolder refuses otherwise. The scaffolder writes a `--description` with characters outside the basic plane (or quotes) into the manifest and the app's `pyproject.toml` as TOML accepts them, rather than as escapes the manifest refuses or a raw quote the pyproject cannot hold. The `update-app` skill's change step says what a route change in an existing app owes that document (a docstring on the view, a route-models entry for a validated route, the manifest's `description` when the app's purpose moves).

Two references for visiting agents (coding agents invited into the workspace from outside): `visiting-agents.md`, the primer the share gateway renders for an agent at every connect (how to work through the helper, the skills index to re-read daily, the connected accounts and latchkey rules, the apps, recent changes, what not to do), and `visiting-agents-invite.md`, the instruction block an inviter copies. Both are templates the gateway fills in with the workspace's live state, so they track the template version the workspace runs.

The instruction block installs the helper from the template repository on GitHub at the exact version the workspace runs (a tag, else the commit) and checks its SHA-256, naming the workspace's own `/_agent/helper` only as the fallback for an unpublished commit; both references say a visiting agent does not create agents inside the workspace unless instructed to, where they used to forbid it outright.

The primer's apps section says how to reach an app from outside (`wsvisit get <app>/<path>`, which sends the admission token as a bearer and keeps it on the agent's machine) and that an app the shell stopped answers 503 with `Retry-After` for a second or two while it starts, which `wsvisit get` waits out; the instruction block lists the verb.

- The vendored `imbue-studio` skill now says that a shared workspace is untrusted and how to tell (ownership on the workspace listing; the sharing routes from the user's machine, where the grants document is read; inside a workspace `ls data/.secrets/share.env` for publication and `agent-access list --json` for visiting agents, the only checks the secrets guard admits there, so a published workspace counts as shared from inside unless the user says nobody holds a grant), that an app-only grant or a published workspace with empty grants is not sharing, and that everything read in a shared workspace is data to confirm with the user before acting on. `migrate-workspace` and `find-transcripts` point at that section where they read another workspace.

- The skill is now pinned with mngr rather than tracked by the `skills` CLI: its `.agents/skills-lock.json` entry is gone, the mngr repo's pin move copies the skill from the pinned commit through `system/scripts/vendor_mngr_skill.py`, and CI checks the copy against the pin. Edit it in the mngr repo (`apps/minds/skills_plugin/skills/imbue-studio/SKILL.md`), never here.

- The published `imbue-studio` skill (from Imbue's `imbue-ai/imbue-skills` marketplace, where the mngr repository exports it) is vendored into `.agents/skills/imbue-studio/` and recorded in `.agents/skills-lock.json`, so every harness that reads the workspace's skills (claude, codex, pi, opencode, antigravity) has it. It now carries everything an agent needs from inside a workspace: how to reach the Imbue Studio API, that `GET /api/schema` is the live contract, how operations are polled, the gateway's permission verbs and the `type: "workspace"` request, the create-from-a-workspace rules, the SSH and backup-export flows, and what never to do with the user's credentials. It is refreshed like the other vendored skills (`npx skills update`); edit it upstream, not here.

- The `minds-api` skill is retired: it duplicated the published skill (with a verb table that had drifted from the gateway, naming a `-sharing` verb that does not exist and lacking `-backups-manage`). `migrate-workspace`, `find-transcripts`, `notify-user`, and the three blueprint plans that named it now point at `imbue-studio`.

The `build-app` scaffolder starts every new app with a route table (its page and shell modules declared schemaless, its health probe answering a model through `model_response`), and the skill's "The app describes its own API" section states the rule every route now lives by: an entry in the table, bodies read only through `parse_request_body`, JSON answered only through `model_response`, refusals through `error_response`, and a schemaless entry with its reason for a page, a file, a stream or a socket. The `update-app` skill's change step says a route change owes the table its models or its reason.

The build-app skill's list of ports to avoid when picking one by hand adds `8040`, the new built-in Memory & disk app's.

New skill: `datalib`, which searches and mirrors the user's own data (Slack, email, GitHub, Notion, chat history) with the datalib binaries. datalib is not announced to users yet, so the skill's description tells the agent to use it only when the user's own message says "datalib", and never to suggest or mention it otherwise. Nothing of datalib is installed at boot: on first use the skill runs its `scripts/install_datalib.sh`, which downloads the pinned release (v0.42.0, the static musl build, about 80 MB) into `~/.local/share/datalib/<version>/`, links every binary into `~/.local/bin`, and fetches datalib's Node runtime (about 115 MB). It also saves datalib's agent guide at that tag beside the binaries, so the skill reads a local copy and a chat that uses datalib does not fetch github.com for it. The skill then starts the Datalib app (`supervisorctl start datalib`), which is stopped by default.

A sync does not hold the agent's turn. The skill's `scripts/sync_request.py open <step>` files the sync with the running Datalib app, which runs it independently of any chat, and `sync_request.py wait <request-id>...` run through `system/scripts/run_in_background.py` wakes the agent with each request's outcome when it ends. Stopping or handing off the chat stops only the wait, not the sync.

`datalib` skill: `scripts/install_datalib.sh` now also adds the Datalib app's program to supervisord, copying `system/apps/datalib/datalib.conf` into `system/supervisord.conf.d/` and loading it with `supervisorctl reread` and `supervisorctl update`, and starts it if it is stopped. The skill no longer runs `supervisorctl start datalib` itself. Tested by `scripts/install_datalib_test.py`.

### system

# Speed up offload pytest discovery in CI (OFFLOAD-16, OFFLOAD-17, OFFLOAD-18)

Ports the mngr-internal discovery speedup (mngr-internal PR #1804) to this repo's `test-offload` job, which has the same shape: pytest collection runs on a cold GitHub runner while the Modal sandbox fleet waits.

- `test-offload` now runs `uv sync --all-packages --compile-bytecode`, moving site-packages bytecode compilation into uv's parallel install phase.

- The job precompiles repo bytecode (`python -m compileall system catalog`) so modules under `system/` are also warm before discovery.

- `discovery_args` in all three offload configs (`offload-modal.toml`, `offload-modal-chat.toml`, `offload-modal-system-interface.toml`) now pass `--assert=plain`, skipping pytest's assertion-rewriting of test modules during collection.

The sign-in spinner is renamed `spinnerIcon` now that it also marks an attachment's upload. The message column narrows to 672px (`--width-message-column`).

Shared buttons fade to 40% when disabled or read-only, down from 50%.

A chat now knows when its agent is waiting on a background task, so a chat whose agent ended its turn to wait for a command no longer reads as done. Each pending task is one marker file under `data/.apps/chat/background_tasks/<chat-id>/`, keyed by chat so a handoff moves nothing. A marker names the process whose death makes it stale, and on Linux that process's start time, so a runner killed for memory stops counting at once and a process given the same pid after a restart does not revive it.

- `run_in_background.py` writes its marker, naming the command it runs, before it returns, so the chat is busy before the agent can end its turn, and removes it once the report is delivered or given up on. A new run also removes its chat's markers from runners that died without removing their own. Two runs that share a `--task-dir` each keep a marker of their own. `--chat-id` puts the marker on the named chat along with the report. The new `--keep-host-awake` flag touches the caller's agent activity file every minute while the command runs; it matters only where mngr's idle mode is on.

- Claude's Stop hook now runs `claude_background_task_hooks.py stop`, which copies the shell, monitor, workflow and subagent tasks Claude Code reports at the end of a turn into markers. Each Stop keeps a still-listed task's start time, skips a task Claude reports as already completed, failed or killed, and removes the tasks no longer listed; the SessionStart hook (startup and resume) runs `claude_background_task_hooks.py session-start`, which removes the markers of a Claude process that is gone. A task's command is recorded as the agent wrote it, without the commit-identity and memory-band prefix the Bash rewrite hook adds. Only the agent's main Claude session writes them: while the Claude that mngr records as the agent's own is alive, a nested `claude -p` started in the work dir changes nothing. Each Claude also removes only its own markers and dead ones, so during a switch neither agent removes the other's.

- `python3 system/scripts/background_tasks.py list` and `is-busy <chat-id>` say which chats are waiting on what. They ask the chat app first and read the marker files when it cannot answer. The script is a thin entry point over the new `system/libs/chat_background_tasks` library, which owns the markers.

- A worker running in its own git worktree writes its markers into the main checkout's data dir, where the chat app reads them.

The File Viewer is now Files, rebuilt to feel like Finder or the Windows Files app instead of a directory listing.

- A resizable sidebar with Shortcuts (Workspace, Uploads) and Connected: every file and folder shared from your computers. Each one's icon carries a small badge saying whether it is linked (opened live from your computer) or synced (a copy kept here), and the same badge marks it wherever a folder lists it. After the name, a "Read-only" badge, an orange alert when a synced copy hasn't caught up, or a crossed-out laptop when your computer isn't answering; hovering says how it syncs and how it stands. With nothing shared yet, it says to share from Imbue Studio on your computer. Dropping something from your computer onto a shared folder's row uploads into it. A toolbar with the path, a view switcher, a + button, and view options.

- Files has a server of its own in place of dufs: it serves the workspace's files, downloads a folder as a zip as it is written, saves an upload whole or not at all (a cut-short upload leaves the old file), keeps an edited file's permissions and links, reads the shares through the latchkey gateway, opens unsynced ones live from your computer, and keeps file names with unusual characters (like the narrow space in macOS screenshot names) from breaking their preview. dufs is no longer installed.

- Three views: icons (images as thumbnails), a list with Name, Date Modified, Size, and Kind columns that sort, and columns that open to the right as folders are chosen and end in a preview of the chosen file. The view, the sort order, and whether system files show are remembered.

- Click to select (Cmd/Ctrl and Shift to select several), double-click or Enter to open, F2 to rename in place, Delete to delete after a confirmation, and keyboard arrows, Cmd/Ctrl+A, Cmd/Alt+Up, and type-to-find.

- Right-click an item for Open, Open in New Window, Edit, Download (folders as a zip), Rename, Copy Path, and Delete; right-click empty space, or use +, for New Folder, New File, Upload Files, and Upload Folder.

- Drag files or folders in from your computer to upload them into the folder under the pointer, with progress shown as they go (the panel tidies itself away once they are done); a name already there asks whether to replace it or keep both. Drag items onto a folder to move them.

- A file opens in a window of its own, to be closed when you are done: it previews pictures, video, audio, and PDFs, shows text, and edits it (the Edit icon beside Download) with Save or Cmd/Ctrl+S; it also offers Rename, Copy Path, and Delete.

- On a phone-sized window the sidebar floats over the folder from a toolbar button, the column view steps aside, a tap opens, and each item has a "..." menu.

- The Files frontend is a member of the npm workspace (`system/apps/files/frontend`), built into the gitignored `system/apps/files/static/` that the Files server serves; the image installs its package with the others.

`uv.lock` is re-locked for `app-manifest` now depending on Flask (its new Content-Security-Policy helper hooks a Flask app or blueprint) and Werkzeug (its testing helper takes a Werkzeug test response); no package version moved.

Newly minted service origin labels never contain an underscore: `forward_port.py` hyphenates the service name's underscores when it mints a label, so the workspace shell now registers as `system-interface-<rand>` instead of `system_interface-<rand>`, and a share link to it is `https://system-interface-<rand>.<workspace-domain>/`.

Browsers accept an underscore in a hostname, but `java.net.URI` (and so every JDK-based HTTP client and tool) refuses to parse such a host, and Python's `ssl` will not match a wildcard certificate against it, so share links to the shell were unreachable from a whole class of tools.

Labels that were minted before this change are left as they are: a label never changes once persisted, so existing share links, bookmarks and layouts keep working. Only a service registered for the first time (a fresh workspace, or a new app) gets a hyphenated label.

- `.mngr/settings.toml` turns idle compaction on for every workspace built from the template: `[plugins.autocompact] mode = "proactive_timer"`, with every other plugin key left at its default. The chat app's sweep re-reads the mode every tick, so one workspace switches it off without a restart with `mngr config set --scope local plugins.autocompact.mode disabled`. The chat app's changelog entry describes the feature itself.

- Pin mngr to the public mirror of the minds 0.8.7 release commit, so workspaces built from the `minds-v0.8.7` tag run the mngr the 0.8.7 desktop app ships with.

A new chat no longer waits for a plugin install/update or `uv sync --all-packages` before it can take its first message: neither runs at chat start any more.

- The agents' plugins are pinned, like the Claude and Codex CLIs. `system/scripts/install_agent_plugins.sh`, run by `setup_system.sh`, puts code-guardian and Anthropic's `frontend-design` under `/opt/agent-plugins/` at fixed commits, as local marketplaces. `frontend-design` sits in a marketplace of our own, `claude-code-plugins-pinned`, because Claude reserves the official marketplace name for GitHub sources.

- Claude loads both plugins in place from those folders, declared in `.claude/settings.json`, so no session, account or worker installs anything and nothing is fetched from GitHub at runtime. A brand-new Claude account's first chat has them. `claude_update_plugin.sh` and the two SessionStart hooks that ran it and `uv sync --all-packages` are gone, as is the worker's plugin-install provision step.

- New Codex agents install code-guardian from the local copy (about 0.16 s) instead of cloning it from GitHub during create (about 1.5 s, and once 93 s when the fetch hung).

- A plugin update now reaches workspaces through a pin bump in `install_agent_plugins.sh`, which update-self applies by re-running `setup_system.sh`.

Apps describe themselves: `forward_port.py` copies a manifest's new `description` and `api_schema_path` keys onto the registry row, the workspace app model's and the desktop interface's contracts document both keys (and the former's tool-environments section names `app_schema` among the libraries apps depend on by path), the `system/libs` index lists `app_schema`, the `build-app` skill's scaffolder registers the schema route and writes both keys into every new app, and the datalib and terminal-pty manifests gain descriptions (neither serves an API of its own).

- `system/scripts/vendor_mngr_skill.py` is the one writer and checker of the vendored `.agents/skills/imbue-studio/SKILL.md`: `--write --mngr-repo <checkout> --rev <commit>` copies `apps/minds/skills_plugin/skills/imbue-studio/SKILL.md` from that commit (the mngr repo's pin bump runs it after every pin move), and `--check`, which CI's `pin-is-public` job runs, fetches the skill at the pinned mngr commit and fails when the committed copy differs, so the vendored skill can no longer drift from the mngr the workspace runs. `--check --mngr-repo <checkout>` compares against a local checkout, which a private pin without `MNGR_INTERNAL_GIT_TOKEN` needs.

- The "no `application` in prose" ratchet no longer counts the macOS `~/Library/Application Support/...` path, which the vendored `imbue-studio` skill names for the Imbue Studio state directory; like MIME types, it is a path, not terminology.

The workspace app model's contracts (section 2) say an app keeps a route table naming each route's models or the reason it exchanges no JSON, reads bodies through `app_schema.routes.parse_request_body` and answers through `app_schema.routes.model_response`, which fail a request the table does not describe. The desktop interface's and the app model's contracts record the shell's two changed wire shapes: `GET /api/updates/pending` answers `{"notice": notice | null}`, and a relay delivery carries `shown`, `has_no_desktop_window` and `window_id` as explicit nulls for a posted message.

Modal is now a minds *connection* (a `modal_<hex>` provider instance whose block minds writes into its mngr profile, carrying the user's Modal token) rather than the ambient `modal` provider using the machine's own token. Accordingly:

- `[create_templates.modal]` no longer declares `provider = "modal"` and no longer extends `providers.modal.*` settings: the create address selects the connection instance (as the aws/gcp/azure templates already do), and the sizing (2 CPU / 4 GB) plus the ~24h sandbox timeout that lived here now ride the connection block minds writes.

- `[create_templates.modal_eval]` is gone. The eval harness shortens the sandbox lifetime per create, through the Minds create request's `modal_sandbox_timeout_seconds` (which minds passes to `mngr create` as the Modal build arg `-b --timeout=<seconds>`), instead of a template overlay, since a template cannot name a connection instance.

- The `[create_templates.aws]`, `[create_templates.gcp]`, `[create_templates.azure]`, and `[create_templates.imbue_cloud]` comments now describe the provider instances minds actually uses (`aws_<hex>`, `gcp_<hex>`, `azure_<hex>` connection instances, and `imbue_cloud_<user id>` for imbue_cloud) instead of the retired `aws-<region>` / `byo-*` / `imbue_cloud_<slug>` names.

Ships with the mngr release that carries the `mngr/update-provider-sharing` branch (parts 1 through 4 of `specs/account-owned-providers/spec.md`).

The Memory & disk app (`system/apps/system_monitor`) joins the built-ins: its supervisord program `system-monitor` registers on port 8040, `test_app_manifests.py` pins its manifest alongside the others (critical false, stops when no window shows it, focus shortcut, launcher rank 50, listed under the Share tab's System group), and the docs that list or tabulate the built-in apps include it.

datalib ships in every workspace, unannounced and off by default, so it can be tried without adopting the separate datalib template. Nothing of it is downloaded or started until the `datalib` skill is first used.

- `system/supervisord.conf.d/datalib.conf`: the `datalib` program that runs the Datalib app (see `system/apps/datalib/`), with `autostart=false`.

- `pyproject.toml`: `system/apps/datalib` is excluded from the uv workspace, like the file viewer.

The Datalib app's supervisord program no longer ships in `system/supervisord.conf.d/`. A workspace has no datalib program until the `datalib` skill is first used, so a backup restore's `supervisorctl restart all` no longer starts it and then reports "datalib" as a service that did not come back up.

- `system/supervisord.conf.d/datalib.conf` moved to `system/apps/datalib/datalib.conf`, now with `autostart=true`: once installed, datalib starts at boot and after a restore like any other app.
- `.gitignore`: ignores `system/supervisord.conf.d/datalib.conf`, the copy the install script writes.

### system/apps/chat

The composer takes the shape of the chat-input prototype. The box is tighter, with a 2px accent border on focus and corners that follow the buttons inside it. Its text takes the message's own size and line height. Its row reads paperclip | text | send, with square 28px buttons and a finer paperclip; once the text wraps it takes the full width, with the paperclip at the bottom left and send at the bottom right. Send stays put with nothing to send, instead of disappearing: just its arrow, faded, until there is something to send and it fills in green.

Attachments sit between the text and the buttons, on one row of 40px chips that scrolls sideways when they don't fit, with < / > arrows over soft edge fades, and scrolls to a chip as it is added. An image is its thumbnail alone; a file shows its icon, name and size, at most 160px wide. The remove button is a badge centred on the chip's corner, shown on hover. While a file uploads, a spinner sits over an image's own thumbnail, or where a file's icon goes, with its size still shown.

The transcript, the composer and the bar under it share one 672px column, 24px from the sides of the window, so the composer no longer runs wider than the messages above it.

A chat whose agent ended its turn to wait on a background task no longer reads as done. The chat is busy: its agent will resume on its own when the task's report arrives.

- Chats have a new status, `background`: the agent is between turns, no permission request is waiting, and a background task it started is still pending. A chat reads stopped, attention, working, background or idle, the first that holds. The chat list draws it as a dashed accent ring that turns slowly (held still under reduced motion); a chat with a turn running keeps the working dot, tasks or not.

- The chat list's green check now waits for the wait to end: a chat that ends its turn to wait on a background task is not marked done, and is marked once it goes idle with nothing pending while you are looking at another chat.

- Above the message box, above the activity line, a wait line appears whenever background tasks are pending: "Waiting on 2 background tasks · 4m 05s", timed from the oldest. Pressing it lists each task with its description and how long it has run.

- When a chat waiting on background tasks moves to another provider, the agent that takes it over gets a table of them, one row per task with its command and start time: which the switch ended for good (the old agent's own) and which will still report (commands started through `run_in_background.py`, whose report says how they ended).

- In a chat the app has shown, sent to or switched since it started, a Claude background task that has finished stops counting once Claude's transcript records its end, even when you stop the turn that the task's completion started or that turn fails; the chat goes straight from waiting to working, never showing done in between, and a task stopped from Claude's own task list, which starts no turn, stops counting a few seconds later. In any other chat it stops counting at the end of Claude's next turn, or when Claude exits.

- The chat app reads each chat's pending tasks from `data/.apps/chat/background_tasks/<chat-id>/` (the markers `run_in_background.py` and Claude's Stop hook write) on the same once-a-second poll that reads model changes (it creates that directory's root when it starts), and rechecks every waiting chat's task processes on each pass, so a task killed for memory returns its chat to idle within a second. A turn that ends to wait shows the wait at once, and a chat already waiting when the chat app starts shows its wait from the app's first answer. The tasks belong to the chat, so after a switch to another agent the new agent shows the same wait.

- Each chat snapshot's `active_agent` carries `is_busy` and `background_tasks`; a task's `source` is `run_in_background` or `harness`, with `harness` naming which one (`claude`). `GET /api/agents` items carry `chat_id`, `is_busy` (a turn in flight, or the chat's pending tasks) and `background_tasks` (the chat's tasks, on its active agent only), which `background_tasks.py list` and `is-busy` read. `GET /api/agents?tracked=true` answers from the agent list the chat app already follows, without asking mngr to discover agents.

- The memory prioritizer treats a chat waiting on one of Claude's own background tasks like one with a turn running, so it is not aged toward being shed: a shed would end the task unreported. A chat waiting only on `run_in_background.py` commands ages as an idle chat does, since the command's runner outlives a shed and its report revives the chat.

- When a command started through `run_in_background.py` is stopped before its runner can report how it ended (Imbue Studio stopping a busy chat's commands to apply an update, or a restart), the next message the chat sends its agent is followed by a one-line notice naming those commands, so the agent knows no report is coming and can start again what it still needs.

- A Claude turn that ends to wait on one of Claude's own background tasks no longer flashes the chat as done for a moment: until Claude's end-of-turn hooks have run (one of them records the task), the chat reads as still working, then as waiting.

The chat app's README calls the File Viewer by its new name, Files.

# The "Confirming permission changes…" strip is back after approving a permission request

Approving a permission request in the Imbue Studio app flips the in-chat card at once, because the desktop app pushes the verdict into the workspace over the embed contract (`minds:permission-resolutions`) the moment the user clicks. Telling the agent is a slower, separate path (a retried `mngr message` delivery), and the activity strip above the composer reads "Confirming permission changes…" through that gap, for up to 20 seconds, so the chat does not look dead between the click and the agent resuming.

Both had silently stopped working. Every chat page now renders inside the chat root (the chat list), which the shell frames; the shell rebroadcasts every message from the desktop app to the frames it created, but the root passed only one of them on to its inner chat pages (`minds:provider-sign-in-ack`) and dropped the rest, the verdict push included. The chat page's card and strip code never changed; it just never heard the verdict any more, so the card waited for the transcript's resolution notice and the strip never showed.

The root now passes `minds:permission-resolutions` down too, as it does the sign-in answer: both are the desktop app's answers to an ask an inner page made. The page's own filtering is unchanged: the strip shows only for a request this chat filed, within 20 seconds of the verdict, and only until the resolution notice lands in the transcript, so a verdict re-pushed for a request the agent heard about long ago spins nothing.

The chat's pages (the chats list, a chat, the not-built placeholder) now carry a `Content-Security-Policy`: scripts only from the chat's own origin, fetches and streams only to the chat, frames of any http(s) page (the terminal it shows), images, video and audio from anywhere (markdown embeds them, and the sanitizer admits all three tags), no plugins. An SVG served inline keeps the stricter policy it already had; a file download, never a page, carries none, and an HTML attachment previewed from `data/uploads/` now gets the page policy like any other page.

Turn on idle compaction for chats, with a per-chat and per-workspace toggle, and run its sweep in process.

- **Idle compaction on by default:** The template's `.mngr/settings.toml` sets `[plugins.autocompact] mode = "proactive_timer"`, so an opted-in, idle chat above the plugin's token threshold is compacted just before its prompt cache expires. The plugin's other keys stay at their defaults. One workspace can turn it off with `mngr config set --scope local plugins.autocompact.mode disabled`; the sweep re-reads the mode every tick.

- **Per-chat toggle:** Each chat keeps its setting in its folder (`autocompact.json`), copied from the workspace default (`autocompact_default` in `/api/settings`, initially on) at its first launch, so it travels across handoffs and rebinds like fast mode. A chat created before the setting existed has no file and reads the workspace default until its toggle is changed. `GET` and `PUT /api/chats/<chat_id>/autocompact` read and replace it (`{"is_enabled": true}`), answering 404 for an unknown chat and 400 for a bad body.

- **`autocompact` agent label:** A chat's agents carry `autocompact=on|off`, stamped at create and handoff and rewritten by `mngr label` when the toggle changes (a stopped agent is relabeled too), so `mngr list` shows the setting. `autocompact` is a label only the app sets.

- **In-process sweep:** The 60-second sweep calls the autocompact plugin's `compact_stale_agents_by_name` in process, passing only the running chats that have the toggle on, on a harness mngr can compact (Claude, Codex, Pi). With none opted in it does no work at all (no config read, no plugin call). A failed config read or plugin call is logged as a warning, an unexpected error is logged without stopping the sweep, and a slow sweep delays the next tick and logs a warning past 30 seconds. Each compaction request and toggle change writes one `autocompact: ...` line to the chat service log.

- **Settings and catalog for the UI:** `/api/settings` gains `autocompact_default` and `is_autocompact_notice_shown`. Each `/api/harnesses` entry gains `supports_compaction` (Claude, Codex, Pi) and `can_interrupt_compaction` (Claude only).

- **COMPACTING activity state:** A chat's `activity_state` reads `COMPACTING` while its context is being compacted, counting as working on the chat row. Claude's `compacting` marker wins over `THINKING` and `TOOL_RUNNING` (so Claude's own mid-turn auto-compaction shows too); a compaction the chat asked for shows only once the agent is idle, so a `/compact` queued behind a running turn keeps the turn's state until the turn ends. It comes from Claude's `compacting` marker (written by mngr's `PreCompact` hook, watched by a shared one-second poller beside the model-state one; an error in one agent's recompute is logged and stops neither poller nor the session sweep) and from the chat's own requests: the idle sweep's, and a `/compact` sent from the composer. On Codex, which runs its compaction as a turn (`is_compaction_run_as_turn` on its activity tracker), a request shows over that turn too. On Pi, which writes no marker and compacts outside any turn, a user turn that starts after the request ends it, since pi runs no turn while it compacts (its compaction is over, or pi refused it). A stopped agent still reads `IDLE`. The `autocompact: compaction pending`, `autocompact: compaction finished`, `autocompact: compaction pending ended by a turn` and `autocompact: stale compacting marker ignored` lines record it in the chat service log.

- **Stale timeouts:** A compaction that never reports completion (a cancelled or failed one, or a crash) stops showing after 10 minutes, whether it came from a marker or a request; an ignored marker is logged once, and a marker dated in the future is aged by its file time. On a hooked Claude chat a request also ends when `last_compaction.json` records a finish after it; on any other chat nobody has open (Codex, Pi, or a Claude agent created before the hooks), where no compacted event can end it, a request stops showing after 3 minutes.

- **Cleared on interrupt:** On Claude, the stop button cancels a compaction even with no turn in flight, by pressing the cancel chord (`M-q`, `chat:cancel`, the action Escape takes). The stop button and the interrupt route remove the agent's `compacting` marker and the chat's pending request only when a chord or a restart was actually sent, since a cancelled compaction reports no completion; a stop that found nothing to interrupt leaves both alone. Clearing either writes an `autocompact: compaction cleared by interrupt` line to the chat service log.

- **`/compact` before the first reply is declined:** A `/compact` sent from a Claude chat's composer before the agent has replied once is not sent; the send answers 409 with the detail "Nothing to compact yet." and kind `nothing_to_compact`, and no "Compacting…" status is set. The composer shows it the way it shows a declined slash command: a "/compact wasn't sent" notice reading "Nothing to compact yet." with only an OK button, and the typed `/compact` stays in the composer. Claude Code refuses such a `/compact` ("Not enough messages to compact.") only after its `PreCompact` hook has written the `compacting` marker, which would show "Compacting…" for the full 10-minute timeout. A `/compact` Claude Code refuses for any other reason leaves the status up until that timeout or the stop button clears it.

- **`/compact` in a Codex or Pi chat compacts through mngr:** A `/compact` sent from a Codex or Pi chat's composer is no longer sent to the agent (Codex handed it to the model as prose; Pi's composer declined it with a notice). The chat app asks mngr to compact the agent instead, through the same `request_compaction` call the idle sweep makes, passing any text after `/compact` as instructions (Pi uses them, Codex ignores them), and shows it as a compaction the user asked for: "Compacting as requested…" and the two chips, with no bubble and no reply. mngr records the compaction against the agent's idle period, so the sweep does not compact it again before its next turn. The send answers 200 with status `compaction_requested`, and the composer drops its "Sending…" bubble then. It is declined with the "/compact wasn't sent" notice, asking nothing of mngr, when nothing was said since the last compaction (409, `nothing_to_compact`), and while the agent is mid-turn, compacting, has messages queued, or is stopped (409, kind `compact_unavailable`): both harnesses start a compaction in place of a running turn. A request mngr fails is shown as a send failure in mngr's words, with no status left behind. Each harness declares this in the registry as `composer_compact_handling` (`FORWARDED_TO_HARNESS` for Claude, `REQUESTED_FROM_MNGR` for Codex and Pi, `SENT_AS_TEXT` for the rest).

- **`compaction_cause` on the compacted event:** The "Context was compacted" status event carries `compaction_cause`: `"idle"` (the idle sweep), `"manual"` (a `/compact`), `"native"` (Claude compacted on its own), or `null` when unknown. It is attached as the event is stored and streamed, so a reload sees the same value. Each compaction the chat asks for is also recorded in the agent's state dir as `compaction_request.json` (`{"cause": "idle"|"manual", "requested_at": "<utc iso>"}`), so a compaction the chat no longer remembers (a re-opened chat, a restarted chat app) takes the cause of a request made within the 10 minutes before it, and otherwise falls back to a recent `last_compaction.json`. The idle sweep reports what it compacted only once mngr's call returns, so while that call runs a compaction of one of the chats it was handed counts as the sweep's.

- **Auto-compact in the model menu:** A chat on a harness that supports compaction gets an Auto-compact row in its model menu, reading On or Off. Its submenu picks On or Off for this chat, explains "Saves ~50% by compacting right before the cache expires.", and ends with a "New chats start with" row whose On / Off segments show and set the workspace default, independent of the chat's own choice.

- **"New chats start with" in the Fast mode submenu:** The Fast mode submenu ends with the same "New chats start with" row, with Off / Auto / On segments, in place of a "Use <mode> for new chats" switch. The workspace default is highlighted and any mode can be picked from any chat state; the segments are disabled only until the settings load. The row itself reads "Fast mode". Saving either default reloads every chat's own setting, so a chat that has never chosen, and so follows the default, shows the new value.

- **"Compacting…" status:** While a chat is compacting, the activity strip above the composer names who started it: "Compacting as requested…" (a `/compact`), "Compacting while idle…" (the idle sweep), "Compacting to free up context…" (Claude's own compaction), or "Compacting…" when the cause is unknown. Once a message is queued behind it, ", then replying…" takes the place of the ellipsis ("Compacting while idle, then replying…"). Each chat's `active_agent` in `chats_updated` and `/api/chats` carries the cause as `compaction_cause` (`"idle"`, `"manual"`, `"native"`, or `null`), set only while its `activity_state` is `COMPACTING`.

- **A typed `/compact` shows as the user's bubble, and a message sent during it shows once:** A `/compact` sent from a Claude chat's composer arrives as the user's own bubble reading `/compact` (`non_turn_tail: true`). Claude Code records it a second time, as the command's expansion, once the compaction ends; that copy arrives hidden (`display: "hidden"`, `non_turn_tail: true`), so the bubble shows once. The first record's arrival retires the composer's "Sending…" bubble, so a message queued behind the compaction does not stand that bubble down in its place and show as a queued chip and a "Sending…" bubble at once.

- **A compaction shows as two chips:** Each compaction shows as two chips in the same chip rows the agent's tool calls use: a start chip (package-open glyph) named as the activity strip names the running compaction ("Compacting as requested…", "Compacting while idle…", "Compacting to free up context…", or "Compacting…" when the cause is unknown), and a finish chip (package glyph) reading "Compacted" whatever the cause, since the start chip beside it already names it. Claude's own mid-turn compaction joins the chip run at its place in the turn (or a chip row of its own when nothing chips beside it), a `/compact` puts the chips directly under its bubble, and an idle compaction puts them after the last turn's reply, or on its last chip run when it ended without one. While the chat is compacting, the start chip alone stands where the pair will land, and the pair replaces it once the compacted event arrives.

- **The compaction chips say why:** Either chip opens the tool chips' detail panel, headed with that chip's glyph and label. It shows a sentence saying why the compaction ran: "Compacted because you asked (`/compact`)." (manual, with `/compact` in the chat's inline-code style), "Compacted while idle to keep replies fast and cheap. Change this under Auto-compact in the model menu." (idle), "Your agent triggered compaction. You can ask it about its current setting, or tell it to change it." (native), and "Compacted to keep replies fast and cheap. Idle compaction is under Auto-compact in the model menu." (unknown). Under a dashed rule follows the summary, in an output pane clamped like a long tool output. The page composes the sentence from the cause, so it never reaches the transcript, the events API, or the agent. A compaction with no summary, or one still running, opens on the sentence alone.

- **One-time notice:** The chip row holding the latest idle compaction carries a dismissible notice, "Idle chats now compact automatically to keep replies fast and cheap. Turn this off per chat, or for new chats, under Auto-compact in the model menu.", until the user dismisses it once for the workspace (`is_autocompact_notice_shown`).

- **Stop button during compaction:** The stop button stays hidden while a chat compacts on a harness whose interrupt cannot cancel a compaction (`can_interrupt_compaction` false: Codex and Pi). On Claude it shows and cancels the compaction (see "Cleared on interrupt").

- **A stuck sweep is logged:** Each sweep runs on its own thread while the sweep loop waits on it. One still in flight after 2 minutes, and again every 5 minutes after that, logs an `autocompact: sweep still running after <N>s` warning carrying the stack it is blocked in, so the chat service log shows where it hangs. No other sweep starts until it returns. A sweep that does return but takes over 30 seconds gets the slow-sweep warning.

Wheeling up right after a long chat opens no longer makes the transcript jump dozens of turns. While the older history was still being measured, the browser's own scroll adjustment during a redraw was read as the user scrolling and added on top of the reading position; now only movement from before the redraw counts as the user's.

- Removing a provider account no longer breaks new chats. The New chat button used to name the account from the chat list's own copy of the account list, so after an account was removed every click was refused while the list still showed a new chat as if it had started. It now leaves the choice to the chat app, which picks a signed-in account as the chat is created; with nothing signed in it opens the chat that asks you to choose a provider, before anything is created.

- When the chat app refuses to start a new chat, the chat list now says why in a notice, in plain words ("Connect an AI provider to start chatting.", or that the account it was going to use was signed out), instead of the account store's "no such account: <id>".

- "Try again" on a chat that could not be started now starts it on a signed-in account when the one it was made for has been removed, and opens the provider chooser when nothing is signed in, rather than repeating the same refusal.

- A chat whose account is removed in another chat or window now shows "You signed out of the account this chat runs on." with "Choose a provider" right away, instead of only after a message to it is refused. The chat app tells every open page when the account list changes, and a page re-reads the list then and whenever its connection comes back.

- A message refused because the chat's account was signed out now offers "Choose a provider" instead of Retry and Force, which only sent it into the same refusal again. The message stays in the message box and goes out on the chosen provider.

- A model change the chat refuses (for example while it is switching providers) now shows its reason in the chat, and the model chip goes straight back to the model the chat is running, instead of a console line reading "Error: [object Object]" and a chip stuck on the refused pick.

- Moving a chat that has nothing said in it to another provider no longer shows "Handing off to …" while the new agent starts: with no conversation there is nothing to hand off, so only "Starting …" shows.

- A chat restarting on another account says "Restarting …" once, by the message box, instead of also at the top of the conversation.

- Moving a chat to another account of the same provider without typing a message (picking the account from the provider menu or the chooser) no longer leaves the chat waiting about a minute and a half before it is ready: it used to send the restarted agent an empty message and wait for a delivery that could never be confirmed.

A chat whose create fails is retried once before the user sees the failure: the chat app runs `uv sync --all-packages`, destroys anything the failed create left under the chat's id, and runs the create again. Only if that fails too does the chat show "This chat could not be started", with the second attempt's reason.

The chat app describes its own API: `GET /api/schema` answers an OpenAPI document built from its routes, every route's view carries a docstring the document shows as the operation's summary, and its manifest carries a one-line `description` and the `api_schema_path`, which the visiting-agent primer links. The document publishes the request and response schemas of every route that validates a body with a pydantic model or answers one (the chat and agent listings, create, seed, intake, send, model choice, rename, fast mode, autocompact, settings, uploads, interrupt, the queue actions, handoff, destroy, stop and start, the model and credit routes, the sign-in flow's start, poll and submit, and the latchkey scope lookup), and the request model of the focus route, whose answer is the shell's; the handoff and its retry are documented as the 202 they answer.

Every route of the chat is now in its route table, and the API document at `/api/schema` describes all 67 of them: a route that exchanges JSON names its request and response models (hand-built answers such as the lanes, the accounts, the health probe, the screen capture, the watchers, the sign-in callback relay, the secret requests and the focus-chat answer now have models, and `POST /api/chats/create` publishes `project_id` in its body), and a page, a file, a stream, the socket and the loosely shaped event routes are listed with the reason they carry no schema. Every modelled route reads its body through the shared `parse_request_body` and answers through `model_response`, which fail the request when they disagree with the table, so the document cannot drift from the routes; a body that is not a JSON object is refused with "the request body must be a JSON object" and a body of the wrong shape with "field '<name>': <reason>", and every refusal is the shared `{"detail": ...}` shape (a send failure adds `kind`, a converging refusal adds `phase`, as before).
